# Rollcall: everything in one file

> Rollcall scans Wayne State's apps and reports each one's PHP image, Laravel version, auth package and PROCTOR result, checked against the dates in CREED's policy. It keeps a snapshot per scan, so you can see drift and an EOL burn-down.

The README and the Markdown twin of every page, joined. The index is https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/llms.txt. Written by Squire's agent-ready kit; do not edit.

---

## README

Source: https://github.com/waynestate/rollcall/blob/HEAD/README.md

## Rollcall

Checks: `composer ci` (the same command runs on GitLab and GitHub).

> Every app answers "present". The ones on PHP 7.4 answer from the back row.

Front page: [`site/index.html`](https://github.com/waynestate/rollcall/blob/HEAD/site/index.html). It is static, with no build step (see `site/README.md`).
On Citadel, the raw-PHP deploy layer in [`deploy/`](https://github.com/waynestate/rollcall/blob/HEAD/deploy/) serves it: a Squire kit whose front controller puts `site/` behind HELMET's security headers. For local development, serve `site/` directly.

Rollcall is the fleet scanner for the Wayne State application stack. For each app it records the PHP image, the
lowest PHP its `composer.json` allows, the Laravel version, the auth package and its version, the PROCTOR result,
and, when the app commits one, the result, Booster version and finish time of Booster's hop record
(`booster-hop.json`). Then it looks up each version by date in CREED's `policy.json`. It keeps one snapshot per
scan, so you can see drift and an EOL burn-down over time. It prunes old snapshots after the retention window
(default 90 days; the newest one always stays).

Rollcall enforces nothing. It never opens an issue, leaves a comment or deploys anything, and it exits `0` whatever
the fleet looks like. The public report has totals only: counts and progress, no app names, owners or rankings. The
per-app list is internal. Like a good attendance sheet, it is for noticing who is missing, not for shaming them.

### Where it sits in the stack

The parts of the Wayne State application stack, and their jobs. WELD is the Laravel starter app that has most of them installed:

| Part | Job |
|---|---|
| WayneUI (project 0) | The interface layer: tokens, components, four consumer paths |
| CREED | The standards and `policy.json`, the dates Rollcall reads |
| PROCTOR | Measures one app against the policy; Rollcall reads its JSON report and never re-runs a rule |
| Preflight | CI templates |
| SESAME | Protocol-neutral auth; Rollcall reports which auth package each app uses |
| HELMET | Baseline runtime and its own optional `/metrics` |
| Pinstripe | The coding standard this repo includes for its Pint and PHPStan settings |
| Sourdough | Starters |
| Rollcall | The fleet census and EOL burn-down |

### How it is built

A framework-free core (`src/`) plus thin entry points that hold no rules:

- `bin/rollcall`: the CLI (`scan`, `report`, `digest`, `drift`, `advisories`, `prune`). One PHP command, so it works the same on Windows, macOS and Linux.
- `public/index.php`: a raw-PHP front controller for `GET /metrics` and `GET /report.json`.
- `src/Laravel/`: a Laravel adapter with a dashboard page, a `/metrics` route and `php artisan rollcall:scan` and `rollcall:prune`.

CREED's policy reader lives under `src/Creed/` (namespace `Waynestate\Rollcall\Creed`) as a generated copy, made
by CREED's `bin/export.php`. CREED is on Packagist now, so the copy can become a `require` of `waynestate/creed`;
until Rollcall switches, the copy stays. To refresh it, run
`php /bin/export.php --namespace='Waynestate\Rollcall\Creed' --to=src/Creed` from a CREED checkout.
`composer creed-copy:check` proves the copy has not drifted (it reads the checkout from `CREED_PATH`); a hand edit
to `src/Creed/` fails that check.

Weekly CREED copy refresh: a scheduled GitLab job (`creed-copy-refresh`, Mondays, an hour after CREED's policy
robot) re-exports the copy from CREED main, rebuilds the versions table and docs, runs `composer creed-copy:check`
and `composer ci`, and pushes to main only when both pass. A red run leaves main untouched. Details in
MAINTAINING.md, "Refreshing the CREED copy".

Data comes in through three interfaces. Each has a fixture adapter, so you can try everything without a live host:

| Source | Interface | Adapters |
|---|---|---|
| Repositories (`composer.json`, `composer.lock`, `booster-hop.json`) | `RepositorySource` | a directory of fixtures; GitLab over PSR-18, tested against recorded responses |
| Runtime image per app | `ImageSource` | a JSON export of the app list from any platform, or Citadel's own registrations export (which adds forced upgrade dates) |
| PROCTOR result | `ProctorReportSource` | a directory of PROCTOR `--format=json` reports |

Rollcall only reads from every source. It writes its own snapshot directory, and digest files only when
`rollcall digest --out` asks for them.

The decisions behind this shape (saved files over live calls, counts in public, one image source, the contract) are
recorded in [DECISIONS.md](https://github.com/waynestate/rollcall/blob/HEAD/DECISIONS.md) and [ADR/](https://github.com/waynestate/rollcall/blob/HEAD/ADR/).

### Install

```
composer require waynestate/rollcall
```

Rollcall 0.1.10 is on Packagist. No extra repository needed. Requires PHP `^8.3`. The CLI is `vendor/bin/rollcall`.

### Quick start

This runs on the fixtures in the repo, so you need no network and no token. Run `composer install` once
(or the Docker line under "Run the checks"), then the commands below.

Linux and macOS (bash):

```
export ROLLCALL_POLICY_FILE=tests/fixtures/policy.json
export ROLLCALL_REPOS_DIR=tests/fixtures/repos
export ROLLCALL_IMAGES_FILE=tests/fixtures/images.json
export ROLLCALL_PROCTOR_DIR=tests/fixtures/proctor
export ROLLCALL_STORE_DIR=var/snapshots
php bin/rollcall scan
php bin/rollcall report
```

Windows (PowerShell, no bash or WSL needed):

```
$env:ROLLCALL_POLICY_FILE = "tests/fixtures/policy.json"
$env:ROLLCALL_REPOS_DIR = "tests/fixtures/repos"
$env:ROLLCALL_IMAGES_FILE = "tests/fixtures/images.json"
$env:ROLLCALL_PROCTOR_DIR = "tests/fixtures/proctor"
$env:ROLLCALL_STORE_DIR = "var/snapshots"
php bin/rollcall scan
php bin/rollcall report
```

`policy.json` is CREED's file; the copy under `tests/fixtures/` is a snapshot for tests. Use the released one in real
runs.

### Commands

```
rollcall scan       [--today=YYYY-MM-DD] [--prune[=DAYS]]
rollcall report     [--format=text|json|prometheus] [--internal] [--today=YYYY-MM-DD]
rollcall digest     [--owner=CONTACT] [--format=text|json] [--out=DIR] [--send] [--today=YYYY-MM-DD]
rollcall drift      --feed=<file> [--component=php] [--today=YYYY-MM-DD]
rollcall advisories --feed=<file> [--today=YYYY-MM-DD]
rollcall prune      [--days=N] [--dry-run] [--today=YYYY-MM-DD]
```

- `scan` scans once and stores `/.json`. A second scan on the same day replaces it. A
   gap in one source (a missing report, a bad image tag) becomes a note on that app, and the scan carries on. A
   refused GitLab token stops the scan loudly instead of producing a flattering partial answer.
  `--prune[=DAYS]` deletes snapshots older than that many days after saving (default: `ROLLCALL_RETENTION_DAYS`,
  90; 0 keeps everything).
- `report` prints the latest snapshot against the policy as of today. `text` is a terminal table, `json` is the
  machine-readable form, `prometheus` is the metrics text (refused unless `ROLLCALL_METRICS_ENABLED=true`).
  `--internal` adds the per-app list; keep that output inside the project.
- `digest` builds the opt-in owner digests (see "Owner digests" below): plain words about only one owner's apps,
  only when something changed since the previous scan. It prints them; `--out=DIR` writes one text file each;
  `--send` mails them, and only when sending is switched on too.
- `drift` compares `policy.json` with a saved endoflife.date v1 product page (for example
  `https://endoflife.date/api/v1/products/php/` saved to a file). A difference is a flag for a person to look at; the
   policy stays the source of truth. Rollcall does not fetch that page itself.
- `advisories` checks each app's locked `laravel/framework` and auth-package versions against a saved Packagist
  security-advisories response (for example
  `https://packagist.org/api/security-advisories/?packages[]=laravel/framework` saved to a file). One line per
  package and version, sorted by package then version: the status (`affected`, `clear` or `no data`), the count and
  the advisory ids, and how many apps hold that pair. A package with no advisory data prints `no data`, never
  `safe`: an absent row proves nothing about the package, and a version nobody can parse says `no data` too.
     Rollcall does not fetch that page itself; a person saves it and `--feed` points at the file. Output is package
  names and counts only: no app ids.
- `prune` deletes snapshots older than `--days` (default: `ROLLCALL_RETENTION_DAYS`, 90; 0 keeps everything). The
  newest snapshot is never deleted, even if it is older than the cut-off, so the dashboard always has data.
  `--dry-run` lists what would go without deleting anything.

Exit codes: `0` ok, `2` tool error (bad option, unreadable policy, a source that refused). There is no `1`: Rollcall
does not gate anything.

### What the report says

- **Apps present and scan notes**: the apps the scan read, then the notes it printed and carried on past
  (`totals.scan_errors` in JSON). Today a note means a source is not configured (no image export, no PROCTOR
  reports). A note is not a failed scan: a source that refuses stops the scan instead.
- **PHP image, declared PHP floor, Laravel**: apps per version, the state from the policy (`active`, `security_only`,
  `eol`, `unknown`), the date security support ends and the days left (negative once past).
- **Auth package and PROCTOR**: apps per auth package, and per PROCTOR result (`pass`, `fail`, `none`).
- **Drift**, counted per kind: `image_eol`, `image_unknown`, `image_below_floor`, `floor_allows_eol`,
  `floor_unbounded`, `eol_past_grace` (past the policy's grace days), `laravel_eol`, `proctor_missing`,
  `proctor_failing`, `override_expired`.
- **Progress**: apps that moved since the previous scan and apps that went from an EOL image to a supported one. In
  the internal view each upgraded app carries the day it landed.
- **EOL burn-down**: for each scan day, how many apps ran an EOL image on that day. It reads the image, not the
  declared floor, so it stays `unknown` until an image export is configured. Each day also carries the same roll
  three ways, counts only: per support state (`states`), per PHP minor of the image (`php_image`, such as
  `{"8.1": 3, "8.4": 9}`) and per Laravel major (`laravel`). Every stored snapshot gets the breakdown, including the
  ones written before it existed, so the history reaches back as far as `rollcall prune` keeps snapshots.

- **Forced image upgrades**: with Citadel's export as the image source, how many apps have a forced base-image
  upgrade pending, how many are due today or earlier, and the next date (`forced_upgrades`). The same counts reach
  `/metrics` (`rollcall_forced_upgrades_pending_apps`, `rollcall_forced_upgrades_overdue_apps` and
  `rollcall_forced_upgrades_next_due_timestamp_seconds`) and ADVISOR's `rollcall_fleet_summary`. The internal
  per-app list carries each app's `upgrade_due`. Zero with any other image source. See
  [docs/guides/citadel.md](https://github.com/waynestate/rollcall/blob/HEAD/docs/guides/citadel.md).

State is never decided in code: it is derived from the dates in `policy.json` by CREED's reader. A version the
policy does not list is `unknown`.

### Configuration

Every setting is an environment variable. `.env.example` holds placeholders; never commit a real token.

| Variable | Meaning | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `ROLLCALL_POLICY_FILE` | Path to CREED's `policy.json` | none (required for `report`, `drift`) |
| `ROLLCALL_STORE_DIR` | Snapshot directory, the only place Rollcall writes | `var/snapshots` |
| `ROLLCALL_SOURCE` | `directory` (fixtures) or `gitlab` | `directory` |
| `ROLLCALL_REPOS_DIR` | Fixture repositories as `//composer.{json,lock}` | none |
| `ROLLCALL_GITLAB_URL` | `https://` base URL of the GitLab instance | none |
| `ROLLCALL_GITLAB_TOKEN` | A GitLab group or project access token (a bot), or a service account's token, with the read_api scope only, the Reporter role and an expiry. The stack's is the group token rollcall-scanner, rotated by the stack maintainer (docs/security.md). Never in git, never logged, never printed | none |
| `ROLLCALL_GITLAB_GROUPS` | Comma-separated group ids or paths; subgroups are included. Ignored when ROLLCALL_GITLAB_PROJECTS is set | none |
| `ROLLCALL_GITLAB_PROJECTS` | Comma-separated full `group/project` paths; when set, only those projects are scanned and no group is listed | none |
| `ROLLCALL_IMAGES_FILE` | Export of the app list: `{"apps": [{"project": "group/project", "image": "php:8.4-apache"}]}` | none |
| `ROLLCALL_CITADEL_EXPORT` | Citadel's saved registrations export, used instead of `ROLLCALL_IMAGES_FILE` (not both): base images plus forced upgrade dates. See [docs/guides/citadel.md](https://github.com/waynestate/rollcall/blob/HEAD/docs/guides/citadel.md) | none |
| `ROLLCALL_PROCTOR_DIR` | PROCTOR JSON reports, one per app: `group/project` is read from `group__project.json` | none |
| `ROLLCALL_AUTH_PACKAGES` | Comma-separated Composer packages that count as an auth package. An entry without a slash matches that package under any vendor (`wayne-cas` matches `anyvendor/wayne-cas`); an entry with a slash matches exactly. First match in list order wins | `waynestate/sesame`, `waynestate/wayne-cas`, `apereo/phpcas`, `jasig/phpcas`, `subfission/cas`, `wayne-cas`, `simplecas` |
| `ROLLCALL_RETENTION_DAYS` | How many days of snapshots to keep; the newest is never deleted | `90` (0 keeps everything) |
| `ROLLCALL_OWNERS_FILE` | Owners file for the digests: `{"owners": [{"contact": "team@example.test", "digest": true, "projects": ["group/project"]}]}`. Rollcall's own, for the stack's projects, is `owners.json` in the repo (roles only); keep another fleet's outside a public repo | none (no digests) |
| `ROLLCALL_DIGEST_MAIL_ENABLED` | Allow `rollcall digest --send` to mail | `false` |
| `ROLLCALL_DIGEST_MAIL_DSN` | Symfony Mailer DSN for sending, such as `smtp://mail.example.test:25`. A secret: never in git, never printed | none |
| `ROLLCALL_DIGEST_MAIL_FROM` | The from address of the digests | none |
| `ROLLCALL_METRICS_ENABLED` | Turn metrics on (`CLI report --format=prometheus` and `/metrics`) | `false` |
| `ROLLCALL_METRICS_TOKEN` | Bearer token a scraper must present | none |
| `ROLLCALL_METRICS_ALLOW` | Comma-separated scraper IP addresses (exact match) | none |
| `ROLLCALL_PUBLIC_REPORT_ENABLED` | Serve `GET /report.json` (public counts only) | `false` |
| `ROLLCALL_DASHBOARD_ENABLED` | Laravel: serve the dashboard page | `false` |
| `ROLLCALL_DASHBOARD_PATH` | Laravel: dashboard URL path | `rollcall` |
| `ROLLCALL_INTERNAL_ENABLED` | Laravel: serve the per-app page at `/apps` (needs your sign-in middleware) | `false` |
| `ROLLCALL_WAYNEUI_CSS` | Laravel: `https://` or absolute URL of WayneUI's stylesheet for the dashboard | none |

To scan GitLab you need the token and either a group or the project allowlist. The narrow way is
`ROLLCALL_GITLAB_PROJECTS`: name the exact `group/project` paths and Rollcall reads only those, never listing a
group. Otherwise set `ROLLCALL_GITLAB_GROUPS`. The token is a GitLab bot or personal access token with `read_api`
only and an expiry, whose user can read only the projects to scan; until it exists Rollcall runs on its fixtures.
Set `ROLLCALL_SOURCE=gitlab` and the GitLab variables. The `rollcall-scan` job in `.gitlab-ci.yml` does this on a
schedule or by hand (see below). Rollcall sends only `GET` and `HEAD`, fetches the two Composer files without
cloning, skips a file whose blob id has not changed, follows `Link` pagination only to the configured host, and
waits out `429 Retry-After`.

#### Run the collector in Docker

No PHP on the machine? The repo ships a `Dockerfile` that builds a small image of the collector. It runs as a
non-root user, writes only to its snapshot folder, and takes every setting from the environment at run time.
Never put a token in the image: the build stays clean, and the token travels with `-e` (or `--env-file`) each
time you run. Two lines, and every app answers present.

Build it, from the repo root (again whenever the code changes):

```
docker build -t rollcall-collector .
```

That reads the `Dockerfile` next to it and tags the result `rollcall-collector`. Then run a scan. Each `-e`
flag is a setting from the table above; for the narrow scan add
`-e ROLLCALL_GITLAB_PROJECTS=group/project,other-group/other-project` and only those projects are read, no group
is listed. The two `-v` flags mount your policy file and snapshot folder so the answer survives the container:

```
docker run --rm -e ROLLCALL_SOURCE=gitlab -e ROLLCALL_GITLAB_URL=https://gitlab.example.test -e ROLLCALL_GITLAB_TOKEN="$ROLLCALL_GITLAB_TOKEN" -e ROLLCALL_GITLAB_GROUPS=your-group -e ROLLCALL_POLICY_FILE=/app/policy.json -v "$PWD/policy.json:/app/policy.json" -v "$PWD/var:/app/var" rollcall-collector scan
```

Next: after a good scan, `var/snapshots/.json` holds the day's attendance, and the same run with
`report` instead of `scan` prints it. On Windows PowerShell, set `$env:ROLLCALL_GITLAB_TOKEN` first and use
`${PWD}` for the mount paths.

#### Scheduled scan on GitLab CI

Rollcall's own repository (on git.wayne.edu, its canonical home) carries a `rollcall-scan` job in `.gitlab-ci.yml`. It
runs `scan` over the 13 stack projects read-only and keeps the snapshot in `var/snapshots/` as a 30 day artifact.
It runs when a GitLab schedule says so, or when a person starts it by hand from the web; without a token it skips
green. It needs three things in GitLab, and on git.wayne.edu all three exist:

1. A token with the `read_api` scope only, the Reporter role and an expiry. The stack's is the group access token
   `rollcall-scanner` on the `enterprise-apps` group, which expires 2027-11-06 (Rollcall prints a note 14 days
   before).
2. A CI/CD variable `ROLLCALL_GITLAB_TOKEN` on the ROLLCALL project: masked and hidden, protected (the schedule
   runs on the protected default branch), and not a file.
3. A schedule on `main`: CI/CD > Schedules, weekly (Monday), with the variable `ROLLCALL_JOB` set to `scan`.

The token is rotated by a role, the stack maintainer, not a named person. The runbook (where the token lives, when
it expires, the five steps, and what to look for in the job log) is "The scanner token and how to rotate it" in
[docs/security.md](https://github.com/waynestate/rollcall/blob/HEAD/docs/security.md).

About reach: a group token reads every project in its group. The project owner chose group reach for the stack's
token; the allowlist `ROLLCALL_GITLAB_PROJECTS` keeps what Rollcall asks for to the 13 projects (it never lists the
group and never asks for another project). If your fleet needs a tighter fence, give a service account Reporter on
just the projects to scan and use its token instead, because only membership limits what a token can read.

Exactly which scope, and why each other scope stays off: `read_api` covers all five calls Rollcall makes (listed
one by one, with the role and the expiry rules, under "The GitLab token, exactly" in
[docs/security.md](https://github.com/waynestate/rollcall/blob/HEAD/docs/security.md)). Not `api`, not `read_repository` (Rollcall never clones), not `read_user`,
not `self_rotate` (the stack maintainer rotates the token, never Rollcall).

### Owner digests (opt-in)

An owner who asks can get a short digest of only their own apps: what changed since the previous scan (an image
upgrade, a new drift flag, one cleared, a PROCTOR result that moved), then where each app stands. Nothing changed,
no digest. Nobody gets one by default, and no owner is ever guessed from commit authors.

1. Point `ROLLCALL_OWNERS_FILE` at an owners file that maps each scanned project to its contacts (a mail address,
   a team alias or a role). An owner opts in with `"digest": true`; leaving the key out means no. The shape is
   `contract/owners.schema.json`.

   ```json
   {
       "$schema": "contract/owners.schema.json",
       "owners": [
           {"contact": "team@example.test", "digest": true, "projects": ["group/project", "group/other-project"]}
       ]
   }
   ```

   Rollcall keeps its own in the repo: [owners.json](https://github.com/waynestate/rollcall/blob/HEAD/owners.json) lists the 13 stack projects the scheduled scan
   reads, all answered for by the stack maintainer. The repo is public, so it names roles and teams, never a person.
   For another fleet, keep that fleet's file next to its snapshots, outside a public repo.
2. After a scan, `rollcall digest` prints each digest with news (`--format=json` for a script, `--owner=CONTACT`
   for one owner). `--out=DIR` writes them as `-.txt` instead, for a mail tool you already have.
   A scanned app that no entry lists is never dropped: every run names it on stderr as "no owner on file", and the
   JSON lists it under `no_owner_on_file`.
3. To have Rollcall mail them itself, install `symfony/mailer`, set `ROLLCALL_DIGEST_MAIL_ENABLED=true`,
   `ROLLCALL_DIGEST_MAIL_DSN` and `ROLLCALL_DIGEST_MAIL_FROM`, and run `rollcall digest --send`. Without all four, it
   sends nothing. Every contact must be a mail address, or nothing goes out at all.

A digest names apps, so it is internal like the per-app list. It uses the report's own states and drift flags, so a
digest and the report never disagree. Schedule it after `rollcall scan` (weekly suits the burn-down).

### WSU values (Playbook)

`ROLLCALL_GITLAB_URL` is a Wayne State value, so it may come from Playbook (`waynestate/playbook`) when the
environment has none. The environment always wins; Playbook only fills what the environment leaves out. The GitLab
token never comes through Playbook and stays an environment variable.

| Setting | Value |
|---|---|
| `ROLLCALL_GITLAB_URL` | The `https://` base URL of the GitLab instance |

Playbook is private and lives on git.wayne.edu. Getting it into your app:

Composer: add the repository to your `composer.json`, then require the package. Composer authenticates to
git.wayne.edu with the token in `auth.json`.

```json
{
    "repositories": [
        {"type": "vcs", "url": "https://git.wayne.edu/enterprise-apps/playbook.git"}
    ]
}
```

```
composer require waynestate/playbook
```

curl (Linux, macOS):

```
curl --fail -H "PRIVATE-TOKEN: $GITLAB_TOKEN" "https://git.wayne.edu/api/v4/projects/enterprise-apps%2Fplaybook/repository/files/playbook.env/raw?ref=main" -o .env.playbook
```

PowerShell (Windows):

```
Invoke-WebRequest -Headers @{ 'PRIVATE-TOKEN' = $env:GITLAB_TOKEN } -Uri "https://git.wayne.edu/api/v4/projects/enterprise-apps%2Fplaybook/repository/files/playbook.env/raw?ref=main" -OutFile .env.playbook
```

Clone:

```
git clone https://git.wayne.edu/enterprise-apps/playbook.git
```

The token is your own: `read_api` for curl, `read_repository` for clone and Composer.

Playbook is private on git.wayne.edu. If you get a 404, ask the Enterprise Applications team for read access.

### Metrics

Metrics are off by default (the stack's metrics rule). With `ROLLCALL_METRICS_ENABLED=true`, `/metrics` serves
Prometheus text built from the latest snapshot (a request never triggers a scan). It needs `ROLLCALL_METRICS_TOKEN` as a bearer token or an address in
`ROLLCALL_METRICS_ALLOW`; with neither set, nobody gets in. Labels are version numbers, state names, drift kinds and
public package names: no app names or personal data. The dashboard JSON is in `grafana/rollcall-burn-down.json`; import
it into Grafana once a Prometheus server scrapes the endpoint. Run `rollcall scan`
on a schedule so the series moves.

Forced image upgrades from a Citadel export come through as three gauges, counts only, in the same style as the
rest: `rollcall_forced_upgrades_pending_apps` (apps with one pending, overdue ones included),
`rollcall_forced_upgrades_overdue_apps` (due today or earlier) and
`rollcall_forced_upgrades_next_due_timestamp_seconds` (midnight of the next date still ahead, only while there is
one). With any other image source the two counts are 0 and the date is absent. The dashboard shows pending and
overdue as two stat panels.

### Laravel

The package registers itself (`extra.laravel.providers`). Publish the config with
`php artisan vendor:publish --tag=rollcall-config`, set the variables above, and schedule `rollcall:scan`. The
dashboard shows counts and progress; the per-app page is a second route that stays off until you enable it, and it
runs behind `rollcall.dashboard.internal_middleware` (default `web` and `auth.sesame`), so an app with no such
middleware fails closed. The page uses WayneUI's class names and takes its stylesheet from `ROLLCALL_WAYNEUI_CSS`.
The `/metrics` route is registered on its own path; if your app already serves `/metrics` (HELMET does), run Rollcall's
on a separate app or leave metrics off.

### Use Rollcall from your coding agent (ADVISOR)

Rollcall ships a module for [ADVISOR](https://packagist.org/packages/waynestate/advisor), the stack's MCP server: three
read-only tools, and a small creed goes with them: every app answers present, the agent may ask, and nobody gets ranked.

Install both packages where the MCP server runs:

```
composer require waynestate/advisor waynestate/rollcall
```

Then name the module in your own manifest file. Rollcall ships none on purpose, so nothing loads by accident:

```json
{
    "modules": [
        "Waynestate\\Rollcall\\Advisor\\RollcallModule"
    ]
}
```

and point `ADVISOR_MODULES_FILE` at that file. The tools read the snapshot store behind `ROLLCALL_STORE_DIR`; with an
empty store each one says so in plain words and names `rollcall scan`.

| Tool | What it answers |
|---|---|
| `rollcall_fleet_summary` | Counts from the latest snapshot: apps by PHP image, declared floor, Laravel line, auth package and PROCTOR result, drift per kind, progress since the previous scan, forced image upgrades (`forced_upgrades`: pending, overdue, next due), and the snapshot date |
| `rollcall_burn_down` | The dated EOL series, one point per scan day, each with its counts per support state, PHP minor and Laravel major; optional `days` (an integer, 1 to 365) keeps only the most recent days |
| `rollcall_supported_versions` | Every version in CREED's policy, grouped by what it says today: active, security only, or end of life |

The tools take no path, command or URL, make no network call, and answer public counts only: the same fields
`/report.json` serves. The per-app list stays internal and never leaves through a tool. Each answer names its source
and its dates.

### Proof

Rollcall's first scheduled scan of the stack on GitLab CI and a rerun over 58 Wayne State applications
(2026-11-06): what ran, what held, what it caught in Rollcall and what it does not prove yet, on the
[Proof](https://github.com/waynestate/rollcall/blob/HEAD/docs/reference/proof.md) docs page.

### Docs

The full documentation lives at [/docs/](/docs/) on the project site: install, guides, reference and checks, built
from `docs/` by Squire's docs builder. Two tables are generated so they cannot drift: the command reference comes
from `php bin/rollcall list --format=json`, and the environment table is scanned out of `src/`, `bin/` and
`config/`.

- `composer docs` rebuilds `site/docs/` from `docs/`; run it after editing a page.
- `composer docs:check` fails when the built site is stale or a generated table has drifted; `composer ci` runs it.

The pages are committed because the deploy server serves `site/` without building. Every page links back to its
Markdown, and the footer stamps the version the docs describe. Roll call: the docs answer present too.

The docs pages wear the front page's look: the same masthead and menu, ruled paper, Caslon titles, the front
page's red section folios (each section of a page opens with its own "§ 1") and the green back cover. To change it, edit `docs/_header.html` (the masthead, links written as if from `site/`) and
`docs/theme/rollcall.css` (the front page's tokens mapped onto the kit's `--dk-*`, plus a derived dark mode), then
run `composer docs`. Never edit `site/assets/docs.css` or `docs.js`: they are Squire's kit and a sync overwrites them.

### Run the checks

Maintainers: how to build, test and release this project, and where its data comes from, is in [MAINTAINING.md](https://github.com/waynestate/rollcall/blob/HEAD/MAINTAINING.md).
Why it is built this way is in [DECISIONS.md](https://github.com/waynestate/rollcall/blob/HEAD/DECISIONS.md) and the ADRs under [ADR/](https://github.com/waynestate/rollcall/blob/HEAD/ADR/).

`composer ci` runs every check: manifest, tests (the contract suite among them), Pint, PHPStan, `composer audit`, a
check that the front page versions table still matches CREED's policy, and a check that the docs site is current.
The contract itself is JSON Schema in [`contract/`](https://github.com/waynestate/rollcall/blob/HEAD/contract/README.md): the report, the stored snapshot and the
image list export. `tests/ContractTest.php` runs the real commands on the fixtures and validates their output
against it, so a field cannot appear or vanish without the contract changing in the same commit. PHP is not needed on the host:

```
docker run --rm -v "${PWD}:/app" -w /app composer:2.10.3 sh -c "composer install --no-interaction && composer ci"
```

(On Windows PowerShell `${PWD}` works as written; in Git Bash use `$(pwd -W)` and set `MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1`.)

The GitLab pipeline (`.gitlab-ci.yml`) and the GitHub workflow (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) both wrap `composer ci`,
on PHP 8.3, 8.4 and 8.5. git.wayne.edu now has an instance runner, and the stack's CI runs on it. Every product in
the stack still strongly recommends a git.wayne.edu instance runner, so that capacity stays there.

The front page has its own accessibility gate (axe-core in Playwright, run in Docker): `scripts/a11y.sh` on Linux
and macOS, `scripts/a11y.ps1` on Windows; MAINTAINING.md says when to run it.

### Security notes

- Read-only toward GitLab and everything else: one gate in the GitLab adapter allows only `GET` and `HEAD`, and a test
  fails if a write verb appears in `src/`.
- The GitLab token is a group or project access token (a GitLab bot), or a service account's token, with the
  `read_api` scope only, the Reporter role and an expiry; the stack's is the group access token `rollcall-scanner`,
  which expires 2027-11-06. It goes in the environment as `ROLLCALL_GITLAB_TOKEN`, never in git, is sent only to the
  configured `https` host, and is hidden from debug output and error messages. `ROLLCALL_GITLAB_PROJECTS` limits
  what Rollcall asks for, not what the token can read; only the token's membership does that. When the source is
  GitLab, `scan` reads the token's own record (`GET /api/v4/personal_access_tokens/self`) and prints a note 14 days
  before it expires, or when it has already expired. The note names the date; the stack maintainer (a role, not a
  named person) rotates the token before its expiry, never Rollcall, following the runbook in
  [docs/security.md](https://github.com/waynestate/rollcall/blob/HEAD/docs/security.md). The check is advisory: a refused, unreachable or unparseable answer prints
  nothing and never fails the scan, and the token value never appears in output.
- Composer files are parsed as data. No `composer install`, script or plugin from a scanned repository ever runs.
- PROCTOR reports, image tags and app ids are outside input: shapes are validated, text is bounded, and terminal output
  strips control characters.
- Every GitLab call, the scope that covers it, and the scopes the token must not have are tabled in
  [docs/security.md](https://github.com/waynestate/rollcall/blob/HEAD/docs/security.md); a test fails if the adapter calls a path that table does not list.

### Where the code lives

The canonical repository is [enterprise-apps/rollcall](https://git.wayne.edu/enterprise-apps/rollcall) on git.wayne.edu. Clone it over SSH as `git@git.wayne.edu:enterprise-apps/rollcall.git` or over HTTPS as `https://git.wayne.edu/enterprise-apps/rollcall.git`; open issues and merge requests there, and tags are made there, by the maintainer, with an approver. GitHub ([waynestate/rollcall](https://github.com/waynestate/rollcall)) is a read-only push mirror of git.wayne.edu: nobody pushes to it, and Packagist reads from it. Roll call: git.wayne.edu? Present. GitHub? A copy of the sheet.

### Contributing

Issues and merge requests go to git.wayne.edu; see Where the code lives above.

Fleet attendance, Wayne State University

## ROLLCALL

Every app answers “present”.

The ones on PHP 7.4 answer from the back row.

Rollcall is the stack's fleet scanner. For each app it records the PHP image, the lowest PHP its `composer.json` allows, the Laravel version, the auth package and the PROCTOR result. Then it looks up each version in CREED's `policy.json`. Every scan is kept as a snapshot, so you can see drift and how fast the EOL apps are going away.

`$ composer require waynestate/rollcall`

**Works alongside [WELD](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/).** Rollcall doesn't go inside your app. You run it on its own to see what every app in the fleet is running, WELD apps included.

[Quick start](https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/#start-title) [Take the roll](https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/#roll-title)

Today's roll sample data

1. kiln-bookingPHP 8.5present
2. tuba-rentalPHP 8.4present
3. pigeon-postPHP 8.3late
4. lunch-ledgerPHP 8.3late
5. abacus-classicPHP 7.4back row

Answered 5 of 5

A sample roll

### Take the roll

Seventeen made-up apps, seated by PHP version with the newest at the front. As you scroll, Rollcall calls each name. The back row answers with a hand in the air.

Sample data · fictional apps · policy as of 2026-10-28

**Sample roll: seventeen fictional apps with their PHP image, Laravel version, auth package, PROCTOR result and the mark Rollcall gives them**

| No. | App | PHP image | Laravel | Auth | PROCTOR | Mark |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Front row PHP 8.5 and 8.4, active |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| 01 | kiln-booking | 8.5 | 13 | sesame | pass | present |
| 02 | tuba-rental | 8.4 | 13 | sesame | pass | present |
| 03 | moth-catalog | 8.4 | 12 | sesame | pass | present |
| 04 | quad-weather | 8.4 | 13 | none | pass | present |
| 05 | greenhouse-log | 8.4 | 12 | sesame | pass | present |
| 06 | sundial | 8.4 | 13 | sesame | pass | present |
| 07 | otter-tracker | 8.4 | 12 | sesame | pass | present |
| Middle rows PHP 8.3 and 8.2, security fixes only |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| 08 | pigeon-post | 8.3 | 12 | phpcas | pass | late |
| 09 | lunch-ledger | 8.3 | 12 | sesame | fail | late |
| 10 | chess-club | 8.3 | 11, EOL | phpcas | pass | late |
| 11 | lost-mittens | 8.3 | 12 | none | none | late |
| 12 | fog-index | 8.2 64 days left | 11, EOL | phpcas | pass | late |
| Back row past end of life |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| 13 | abacus-classic | 7.4 | 8, EOL | phpcas | none | back row |
| 14 | punch-card-pal | 7.4 | none | none | none | back row |
| 15 | dial-up-directory | 8.1 | 10, EOL | phpcas | fail | back row |
| 16 | floppy-archive | 8.0 | 9, EOL | sesame | pass | back row |
| 17 | ghost-kiosk | legacy-base no version in the tag | none | none | none | inaudible |

- **present**: 7
- **late**: 5
- **back row**: 4
- **inaudible**: 1
- **Answered**: 17

Nobody is marked absent. If one source has a gap, like a missing PROCTOR report or a bad image tag, that app gets a note and the scan carries on. The public report only shows totals like these. The per-app list is the internal view (`--internal`), and it stays inside the project.

Five answers per app

### What “present” means

Four of the answers are versions, and Rollcall looks each one up by date in CREED's `policy.json`. No support date is written into Rollcall's code. The fifth answer is PROCTOR's own result.

1. ### PHP image
   The image the app actually runs on, read from its tag in the app list.
2. ### PHP floor
   The lowest PHP its `composer.json` allows. `*` counts as no floor at all.
3. ### Laravel
   The version that's installed, read from `composer.lock`.
4. ### Auth package
   Which sign-in package is installed: SESAME, a CAS client, or none.
5. ### PROCTOR
   `pass`, `fail` or `none`, from PROCTOR's JSON report. Rollcall never re-runs a rule.

Key to the marks

- present `active`: fully supported
- late `security_only`: security fixes only, and the end date is set
- back row `eol`: past its security date, or older than anything the policy lists
- inaudible `unknown`: newer than the policy knows, or a tag nobody can read

**Supported versions from CREED's policy.json: runtime or tool, version, support state and end of support**

| Runtime or tool | Version | Support state | End of support |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| php | 8.1 | eol_grace_expired | 2025-12-31 |
| php | 8.2 | security | 2026-12-31 |
| php | 8.3 | security | 2027-12-31 |
| php | 8.4 | active | 2028-12-31 |
| php | 8.5 | active | 2029-12-31 |
| laravel | 10 | eol_grace_expired | 2025-02-04 |
| laravel | 11 | eol_grace_expired | 2026-03-12 |
| laravel | 12 | security | 2027-02-24 |
| laravel | 13 | active | 2028-03-17 |
| node | 20 | eol_grace_expired | 2026-04-30 |
| node | 22 | security | 2027-04-30 |
| node | 24 | security | 2028-04-30 |
| node | 26 | active | 2029-04-30 |
| mysql | 5.6 | eol_grace_expired | 2021-02-28 |
| mysql | 5.7 | eol_grace_expired | 2023-10-31 |
| mysql | 8.0 | eol_grace_expired | 2026-04-30 |
| mysql | 8.4 | active | 2032-04-30 |
| mysql | 9.7 | active | 2034-04-30 |
| vue | 2 | eol_grace_expired | 2023-12-31 |
| vue | 3 | active | n/a |
| inertia | 2 | active | n/a |
| inertia | 3 | active | n/a |
| composer | 2.8.0 | minimum | n/a |

Drift and the burn-down

### Watch the back row empty

Rollcall keeps one snapshot per scan day. Count the apps on an EOL image in each one and you get a line that should only go down.

Apps on an EOL PHP image, one scan a week Sample data

Grafana draws the same line from `/metrics` with the bundled dashboard, `grafana/rollcall-burn-down.json`. Each scan day also counts the roll per PHP minor, Laravel major and support state, so the JSON report shows which lines the fleet is leaving and which it is joining.

#### Drift, counted per kind

- `image_eol`runs on an EOL PHP image
- `image_unknown`an image tag nobody can read
- `image_below_floor`the image is older than the app allows
- `floor_allows_eol`the PHP floor still lets an EOL version in
- `floor_unbounded`no PHP floor declared at all
- `eol_past_grace`past the policy's grace days
- `laravel_eol`Laravel past its security date
- `proctor_missing`no PROCTOR report on file
- `proctor_failing`PROCTOR says fail
- `override_expired`a PROCTOR override ran out

`rollcall drift` also compares the policy with a saved endoflife.date page. A difference is a flag for a person; the policy stays the source of truth.

From a checkout, with the bundled fixtures

### Quick start

This runs on the fixtures in the repo, so you need no network and no token, just PHP 8.3 or newer. Run `composer install` once, then the commands below.

**Linux and macOS**

bash

```
export ROLLCALL_POLICY_FILE=tests/fixtures/policy.json
export ROLLCALL_REPOS_DIR=tests/fixtures/repos
export ROLLCALL_IMAGES_FILE=tests/fixtures/images.json
export ROLLCALL_PROCTOR_DIR=tests/fixtures/proctor
export ROLLCALL_STORE_DIR=var/snapshots
php bin/rollcall scan
php bin/rollcall report
```

**Windows**

PowerShell, no bash or WSL needed

```
$env:ROLLCALL_POLICY_FILE = "tests/fixtures/policy.json"
$env:ROLLCALL_REPOS_DIR = "tests/fixtures/repos"
$env:ROLLCALL_IMAGES_FILE = "tests/fixtures/images.json"
$env:ROLLCALL_PROCTOR_DIR = "tests/fixtures/proctor"
$env:ROLLCALL_STORE_DIR = "var/snapshots"
php bin/rollcall scan
php bin/rollcall report
```

What comes back real output, Rollcall 0.1, bundled fixtures (four demo apps)

```
Present: 4 apps. Snapshot 2026-10-28 saved to var/snapshots.

ROLLCALL 0.1.10 | scan 2026-10-28 | as of 2026-10-28 | public
Apps present: 4 (scan notes: 0)

PHP image
VERSION  APPS  STATE          SECURITY UNTIL  DAYS TO EOL
8.1      1     eol            2025-12-31      -301
8.3      1     security_only  2027-12-31      429
8.4      1     active         2028-12-31      795
unknown  1     unknown        -               -

EOL burn-down (state on each scan day)
DATE        APPS  EOL  SUPPORTED  UNKNOWN
2026-10-28  4     1    2          1
```

**exit 0**, however the fleet looks. There is no exit 1: Rollcall takes attendance, it does not hand out detention.

- **`rollcall scan`**: Scans once and saves `<date>.json`. A second scan on the same day replaces it.
- **`rollcall report`**: `--format=text|json|prometheus`. `--internal` adds the per-app list; keep that inside the project.
- **`rollcall drift`**: `--feed=<file>`, a saved endoflife.date page. Rollcall never fetches it itself.
- **In Laravel**: The package registers itself. Publish the config with `php artisan vendor:publish --tag=rollcall-config`, then schedule `php artisan rollcall:scan`.

Left on the desk for your agent

### Notes for the substitute

Your coding agent is the substitute teacher here: it has never met this class. Each note tells it where to read up on Rollcall and what it must leave alone, and asks it to check with you before it guesses. Copy one, or open it in OpenCode, Claude Code, Codex or ChatGPT.

#### Get started with Rollcall

Call the sample roll from a checkout, with the bundled fixtures, and have the agent read the report back to you.

A prompt for your coding agent. Copy it as it stands:

```text
You are a coding agent helping a Wayne State University developer try Rollcall, the fleet scanner of WELD, the Wayne State application stack. Rollcall reads each app's composer.json and composer.lock, its PHP image and its PROCTOR report, and checks every version against CREED's policy.json by date. It enforces nothing and always exits 0.

Read first:
- https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/llms.txt, the index of Rollcall's pages, each one as Markdown. Work from them, not from memory.
- ADVISOR, the stack's MCP server, if it is connected: get_project_status and read_project_docs with project rollcall, and policy_lookup for PHP. If it is not connected, say so and work from the pages. How to add it: https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/llms.txt
- The README in this folder, if this folder is a Rollcall checkout. If it is not, ask me whether to clone https://github.com/waynestate/rollcall first.

Task:
1. Install the dependencies once with `composer install` (PHP 8.3 or newer). If the host has no PHP, use the Docker line in the README's Run the checks section.
2. Point Rollcall at the bundled fixtures: set ROLLCALL_POLICY_FILE, ROLLCALL_REPOS_DIR, ROLLCALL_IMAGES_FILE, ROLLCALL_PROCTOR_DIR and ROLLCALL_STORE_DIR the way the README's Quick start does.
3. Call the roll with `php bin/rollcall scan`, then print it with `php bin/rollcall report`.
4. Read the report back to me: each PHP image, the state CREED gives it, and the days left before end of life.

Constraints:
- Fixtures only: no network and no GitLab token. A real scan needs a read_api group or project access token (a GitLab bot), which a role, the stack maintainer, makes and rotates; never invent one.
- Give separate commands for Windows (PowerShell), macOS and Linux wherever they differ.
- The per-app list (report --internal) stays inside the project. Never paste app names anywhere public.
- Ask me before you guess, and before you touch anything outside this folder.

Output: the commands you ran, the report, then a short reading of it and your questions.
```

#### Or leave the note for your kind of app

#### Rollcall as a plain PHP tool

The CLI on a schedule, and the /metrics and /report.json front controller only if you ask for them.

A prompt for your coding agent. Copy it as it stands:

```text
You are a coding agent setting up Rollcall, the fleet scanner of WELD, the Wayne State application stack, as a plain PHP tool with no framework: a scan on a schedule from the command line and, only if I ask, the /metrics and /report.json endpoints.

Read first:
- https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/llms.txt, then the README it links: the Commands, Configuration and Metrics sections.

2. Write the settings as environment variables from the README's Configuration table: the policy file, the store folder and the source. Start with directory fixtures; switch to GitLab only once the read_api token exists (the stack maintainer makes it) and you have the group.
3. Schedule the scan subcommand once a day with --prune, and show me the report subcommand in text and in json.
4. Only if I ask for metrics: serve the package's public/index.php front controller, with ROLLCALL_METRICS_ENABLED and either ROLLCALL_METRICS_TOKEN or ROLLCALL_METRICS_ALLOW set.

- Rollcall is read-only toward every source and writes only its snapshot folder (plus digest files, when `rollcall digest --out` is asked for). Keep it that way.
- The GitLab token is a read_api group or project access token (a GitLab bot) that the stack maintainer makes and rotates; it comes from the environment as ROLLCALL_GITLAB_TOKEN. Never commit it, log it or print it.
- Metrics and the public report stay off unless I turn them on.
- Give separate commands for Windows (PowerShell), macOS and Linux wherever they differ, schedules included.
- Ask me before you guess, and before you touch a deploy or a scheduler.

```

#### Rollcall in a Laravel app

The scheduled scan and the dashboard of totals. The dashboard is the package's own Blade page, whatever your app renders with.

A prompt for your coding agent. Copy it as it stands:

```text
You are a coding agent adding Rollcall, the fleet scanner of WELD, the Wayne State application stack, to a Laravel app: the scheduled scan, the dashboard page of totals and, only if I ask, the internal per-app page.

Read first:

- composer.json, composer.lock, config/, routes/, bootstrap/app.php and .env.example.

2. Publish the config with `php artisan vendor:publish --tag=rollcall-config`, and add the settings to .env.example as placeholders.
3. Schedule `php artisan rollcall:scan` once a day.

- Meet each setting the Laravel way (config, the scheduler, middleware) before writing code of your own.
- If this app already serves /metrics (HELMET does), leave Rollcall's metrics off.
- Never commit a real token or a .env file.
- Ask me before you guess, and before you touch migrations, auth or anything that deploys.

Output: the files you changed, the scheduler entry, then your questions.
```

Your agent reads the same pages you do. [llms.txt](https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/llms.txt) lists them, [llms-full.txt](https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/llms-full.txt) has all of them in one file, and this page has a [Markdown twin](https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/index.md). The buttons only copy text or open the tool you pick; nothing is sent anywhere.

Classroom rules

### For noticing who is missing, not for shaming them

1. ### It enforces nothing.
   It never opens an issue, leaves a comment or deploys anything, and it exits `0` whatever it finds.
2. ### The public report has totals only.
   Counts and progress. There are no app names, owners or rankings in it.
3. ### It only reads.
   `GET` and `HEAD` only, and a test fails if a write verb shows up in `src/`. It writes its own snapshot folder, and digest files only when you ask.
4. ### Metrics stay off until you turn them on.
   Once they're on, `/metrics` needs a bearer token or an allowed address. If neither is set, nobody gets in.

Three sources and a policy

### Where the answers come from

Rollcall reads three sources plus CREED's policy, and writes one snapshot per scan day. Each source also has a fixture adapter, so you can try all of it without a live GitLab.

- Repositories`composer.json` and `.lock`, from GitLab or a folder
- App listthe PHP image each app runs
- [PROCTOR](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/) one JSON report per app
- [CREED](https://creed.apps.wayne.edu/) `policy.json`, the dates

Rollcall scans and compares

- Terminal`text` and `json` reports
- /metricsPrometheus text, off by default
- Grafanathe bundled burn-down dashboard
- Laravel pagea WayneUI dashboard of totals

Rollcall's place in the stack

### The class list

These are the parts of the Wayne State application stack, and what each one has to do with Rollcall. WELD is the Laravel starter app that has most of them installed.

1. [WayneUI](https://wayneui.apps.wayne.edu/)the interface; the dashboard wears its classes
2. [CREED](https://creed.apps.wayne.edu/)writes the dates Rollcall reads
3. [PROCTOR](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/)checks one app; Rollcall collects the results
4. [Preflight](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/)CI templates, where PROCTOR reports are born
5. [SESAME](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/)the auth package Rollcall counts
6. [HELMET](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/)baseline runtime, with its own `/metrics`
7. [Pinstripe](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/)the Pint and PHPStan rules this repo wears
8. [Sourdough](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/)starters that begin in the front row
9. [WELD](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/)the Laravel starter app, with the stack already set up
10. Rollcallyou are here: the fleet census and EOL burn-down
11. [Booster](https://booster.apps.wayne.edu/)moves the back row forward
12. [Squire](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/)carries the release to Citadel
13. [Drawbridge](https://drawbridge.apps.wayne.edu/)the planned sign-in gateway for Citadel
14. [ADVISOR](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/)the MCP server your agent asks about the stack

## How it is built[#](https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/docs/architecture.html#how-it-is-built)

This page shows the moving parts. Next: [security notes](https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/docs/security.html).

A framework-free core (`src/`) plus thin entry points that hold no rules:

- `bin/rollcall`: the CLI (`scan`, `report`, `digest`, `drift`, `advisories`, `prune`). One PHP command, so it works the same on Windows, macOS and Linux.
- `public/index.php`: a raw-PHP front controller for `GET /metrics` and `GET /report.json`.
- `src/Laravel/`: a Laravel adapter with a dashboard page, a `/metrics` route and `php artisan rollcall:scan` and `rollcall:prune`.

CREED's policy reader lives under `src/Creed/` (namespace `Waynestate\Rollcall\Creed`) as a generated copy, made by CREED's `bin/export.php`. CREED is on Packagist now, so the copy can become a `require` of `waynestate/creed`; until Rollcall switches, the copy stays. To refresh it, run `php <creed>/bin/export.php --namespace='Waynestate\Rollcall\Creed' --to=src/Creed` from a CREED checkout. `composer creed-copy:check` proves the copy has not drifted (it reads the checkout from `CREED_PATH`); a hand edit to `src/Creed/` fails that check.

Weekly CREED copy refresh: a scheduled GitLab job (`creed-copy-refresh`, Mondays, an hour after CREED's policy robot) re-exports the copy from CREED main, rebuilds the versions table and docs, runs `composer creed-copy:check` and `composer ci`, and pushes to main only when both pass. A red run leaves main untouched. The steps are in [Scripts on every OS](https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/scripts.html#inside-gitlab-ci-only).

Data comes in through three interfaces. Each has a fixture adapter, so you can try everything without a live host:

| Source | Interface | Adapters |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Repositories (`composer.json`, `composer.lock`) | `RepositorySource` | a directory of fixtures; GitLab over PSR-18, tested against recorded responses |
| Runtime image per app | `ImageSource` | a JSON export of the app list from any platform, or Citadel's own registrations export (which adds forced upgrade dates) |
| PROCTOR result | `ProctorReportSource` | a directory of PROCTOR `--format=json` reports |

Rollcall only reads from every source. It writes its own snapshot directory, and digest files only when `rollcall digest --out` asks for them.

The decisions behind this shape (saved files over live calls, counts in public, one image source, the contract) are recorded in [DECISIONS.md](https://github.com/waynestate/rollcall/blob/main/DECISIONS.md) and [ADR/](https://github.com/waynestate/rollcall/tree/main/ADR).

---

Source: https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/docs/checks.html

## Run the checks[#](https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/docs/checks.html#run-the-checks)

This page shows how the project is built, tested and released, and where changes land.

Checks: `composer ci` (the same command runs on GitLab and GitHub).

Maintainers: how to build, test and release this project, and where its data comes from, is in [MAINTAINING.md](https://github.com/waynestate/rollcall/blob/main/MAINTAINING.md).

`composer ci` runs every check: manifest, tests (the [contract suite](https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/contract.html) among them), Pint, PHPStan, `composer audit`, a check that the front page versions table still matches CREED's policy, and a check that the docs site is current. PHP is not needed on the host:

```
docker run --rm -v "${PWD}:/app" -w /app composer:2.10.3 sh -c "composer install --no-interaction && composer ci"
```

(On Windows PowerShell `${PWD}` works as written; in Git Bash use `$(pwd -W)` and set `MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1`.)

The GitLab pipeline (`.gitlab-ci.yml`) and the GitHub workflow (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) both wrap `composer ci`, on PHP 8.3, 8.4 and 8.5. git.wayne.edu now has an instance runner, and the stack's CI runs on it. Every product in the stack still strongly recommends a git.wayne.edu instance runner, so that capacity stays there.

The front page has its own accessibility gate (axe-core in Playwright, run in Docker): `scripts/a11y.sh` on Linux and macOS, `scripts/a11y.ps1` on Windows; [MAINTAINING.md](https://github.com/waynestate/rollcall/blob/main/MAINTAINING.md) says when to run it.

### Contributing[#](https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/docs/checks.html#contributing)

The canonical repository is [enterprise-apps/rollcall](https://git.wayne.edu/enterprise-apps/rollcall) on git.wayne.edu; changes land there first, and Wayne State developers open issues and merge requests on that project. GitHub ([waynestate/rollcall](https://github.com/waynestate/rollcall)) is a read-only push mirror of git.wayne.edu: nobody pushes to it, and Packagist reads from it.

License: MIT, Copyright Wayne State University.

Source: https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/advisor.html

## Use Rollcall from your coding agent (ADVISOR)[#](https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/advisor.html#use-rollcall-from-your-coding-agent-advisor)

This page installs the ADVISOR module and names the three tools. Next: [run the checks](https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/docs/checks.html).

Rollcall ships a module for [ADVISOR](https://packagist.org/packages/waynestate/advisor), the stack's MCP server: three read-only tools, and a small creed goes with them: every app answers present, the agent may ask, and nobody gets ranked.

Install both packages where the MCP server runs:

```
composer require waynestate/advisor waynestate/rollcall
```

Then name the module in your own manifest file. Rollcall ships none on purpose, so nothing loads by accident:

```json
{
    "modules": [
        "Waynestate\\Rollcall\\Advisor\\RollcallModule"
    ]
}
```

and point `ADVISOR_MODULES_FILE` at that file. The tools read the snapshot store behind `ROLLCALL_STORE_DIR`; with an empty store each one says so in plain words and names `rollcall scan`.

| Tool | What it answers |
| --- | --- |
| `rollcall_fleet_summary` | Counts from the latest snapshot: apps by PHP image, declared floor, Laravel line, auth package and PROCTOR result, drift per kind, progress since the previous scan, forced image upgrades (`forced_upgrades`: pending, overdue, next due), and the snapshot date |
| `rollcall_burn_down` | The dated EOL series, one point per scan day, each with its counts per support state, PHP minor and Laravel major; optional `days` (an integer, 1 to 365) keeps only the most recent days |
| `rollcall_supported_versions` | Every version in CREED's policy, grouped by what it says today: active, security only, or end of life |

The tools take no path, command or URL, make no network call, and answer public counts only: the same fields `/report.json` serves. The per-app list stays internal and never leaves through a tool. Each answer names its source and its dates.

---

Source: https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/citadel.html

## Citadel's registrations export[#](https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/citadel.html#citadel-s-registrations-export)

This page shows how Rollcall reads the runtime image of each app, and any forced upgrade date, from a file Citadel produces. Next: [run the collector in Docker](https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/collector-docker.html).

Citadel is one source among others. On OpenShift, Coolify or plain Docker, keep using the image list (`ROLLCALL_IMAGES_FILE`), which any platform can produce. Nothing in Rollcall needs Citadel.

### 1. Rollcall never calls Citadel[#](https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/citadel.html#1-rollcall-never-calls-citadel)

Rollcall reads a saved file. It holds no Citadel account, opens no connection to Citadel, and sends nothing back. A person or a scheduled job saves the export, and `rollcall scan` reads it, the same way it reads PROCTOR's reports and the endoflife.date page. If Citadel offers a read-only endpoint that answers with this JSON, save its answer to the file: the shape is the same.

### 2. The shape[#](https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/citadel.html#2-the-shape)

The export uses Citadel's own field names, so the people who keep Citadel can produce it without a mapping table. The schema is `contract/citadel-export.schema.json`; extra fields are ignored, so an export may carry more.

```json
{
    "applications": [
        {"repository": "group/project", "base_image": "citadel/php-apache:8.4r5"},
        {"repository": "group/old-project", "base_image": "citadel/php-apache:8.1r2"}
    ],
    "base_image_upgrades": [
        {"old_image": "citadel/php-apache:8.1r2", "new_image": "citadel/php-apache:8.4r5", "due_date": "2026-12-15", "completed": false}
    ]
}
```

| Field | What it is in Citadel | What Rollcall does with it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `applications[].repository` | The GitLab `group/project` an application deploys from | Joins the app to the repository the scan read |
| `applications[].base_image` | The base image of the application's active deployment | Reads the PHP version (`8.4r5` is PHP 8.4) |
| `base_image_upgrades[].old_image` | The image being retired | Every app on that image gets the due date |
| `base_image_upgrades[].due_date` | The day Citadel forces the upgrade, `YYYY-MM-DD` | The earliest pending date per image counts |
| `base_image_upgrades[].completed` | Whether that upgrade is done | Only `false` counts; a done upgrade is ignored |

Two fields are optional: `applications[].php_version` (the PHP version in the running container, such as `8.3.14`) and `applications[].httpd_version` (the Apache httpd version, such as `2.4.62`). We have asked the Citadel team to send them. When they arrive, Rollcall keeps them in the snapshot and shows them per app in the internal report as "PHP (running)" and "httpd (running)", blank until Citadel sends them; an export without them changes nothing.

Entries Rollcall cannot trust are skipped, never guessed: an application with no repository, an upgrade with no real date (`"soon"`, `2026-02-30`) or without `"completed": false`. An app registered on Citadel but not in the scan is not invented either: the census starts from the repositories.

### 3. Point Rollcall at it[#](https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/citadel.html#3-point-rollcall-at-it)

macOS and Linux

```sh
export ROLLCALL_CITADEL_EXPORT=/path/to/citadel-export.json
php bin/rollcall scan
php bin/rollcall report
```

Windows

```powershell
$env:ROLLCALL_CITADEL_EXPORT = "C:\path\to\citadel-export.json"
php bin/rollcall scan
php bin/rollcall report
```

Set `ROLLCALL_CITADEL_EXPORT` or `ROLLCALL_IMAGES_FILE`, not both: each is a complete image source, and the scan stops with a plain message if both are set. In Laravel, the setting is `rollcall.citadel_export`.

### 4. What the report gains[#](https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/citadel.html#4-what-the-report-gains)

- **Forced image upgrades**: the text report prints `Forced image upgrades pending: 2 (1 due today or earlier), next due 2026-12-15.` and the JSON report carries `forced_upgrades` with `pending`, `overdue` (due today or earlier) and `next_due` (the next future date, or `null`). Counts only, so it is public. With the image list, or no image source, all three are zero.
- **Metrics and ADVISOR**: the same counts reach `/metrics` as `rollcall_forced_upgrades_pending_apps`, `rollcall_forced_upgrades_overdue_apps` and `rollcall_forced_upgrades_next_due_timestamp_seconds` (see [metrics](https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/metrics.html)), and ADVISOR's `rollcall_fleet_summary` tool answers with `forced_upgrades` (see [ADVISOR](https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/advisor.html)).
- **Per app, internally**: the internal report's per-app list carries `upgrade_due`, and the stored snapshot keeps it. Snapshots written before it existed load as `null`.
- **Owner digests**: a new forced upgrade date is news, and so is one that went away. See [owner digests](https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/digest.html).

The export names applications, so keep it where you keep the snapshots: on the host, outside git.

---

Source: https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/collector-docker.html

## Run the collector in Docker[#](https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/collector-docker.html#run-the-collector-in-docker)

This page builds the collector image and runs a scan in Docker. Next: [WSU values (Playbook)](https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/wsu-values.html) for where the GitLab URL comes from.

No PHP on the machine? The repo ships a `Dockerfile` that builds a small image of the collector. It runs as a non-root user, writes only to its snapshot folder, and takes every setting from the environment at run time. Never put a token in the image: the build stays clean, and the token travels with `-e` (or `--env-file`) each time you run. Two lines, and every app answers present.

Build it, from the repo root (again whenever the code changes):

```
docker build -t rollcall-collector .
```

That reads the `Dockerfile` next to it and tags the result `rollcall-collector`. Then run a scan. Each `-e` flag is a setting from [the configuration table](https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/configuration.html); for the narrow scan add `-e ROLLCALL_GITLAB_PROJECTS=group/project,other-group/other-project` and only those projects are read, no group is listed. The two `-v` flags mount your policy file and snapshot folder so the answer survives the container:

```
docker run --rm -e ROLLCALL_SOURCE=gitlab -e ROLLCALL_GITLAB_URL=https://gitlab.example.test -e ROLLCALL_GITLAB_TOKEN="$ROLLCALL_GITLAB_TOKEN" -e ROLLCALL_GITLAB_GROUPS=your-group -e ROLLCALL_POLICY_FILE=/app/policy.json -v "$PWD/policy.json:/app/policy.json" -v "$PWD/var:/app/var" rollcall-collector scan
```

Next: after a good scan, `var/snapshots/<today>.json` holds the day's attendance, and the same run with `report` instead of `scan` prints it. On Windows PowerShell, set `$env:ROLLCALL_GITLAB_TOKEN` first and use `${PWD}` for the mount paths.

---

Source: https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/digest.html

## Owner digests[#](https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/digest.html#owner-digests)

This page shows how an owner who asks gets a digest of only their own apps. Next: [metrics](https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/metrics.html).

A digest is a short note in plain words: what changed in that owner's apps since the previous scan, then where each app stands. Nothing changed, no digest. Nobody gets one by default, and Rollcall never guesses an owner from commit authors.

### 1. Say who answers for which apps[#](https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/digest.html#1-say-who-answers-for-which-apps)

An owners file maps each scanned project to the contacts who answer for it. Point `ROLLCALL_OWNERS_FILE` at it. An owner opts in with `"digest": true`; leaving the key out means no.

```json
{
    "$schema": "contract/owners.schema.json",
    "owners": [
        {"contact": "team@example.test", "digest": true, "projects": ["group/project", "group/other-project"]},
        {"contact": "another-team@example.test", "projects": ["group/third-project"]}
    ]
}
```

Here the first team gets digests and the second does not. A contact is a mail address, a team alias or a role; each one is listed once, and a project may sit under more than one contact. The shape is `contract/owners.schema.json`, and the optional `"$schema"` line lets an editor check the file as you type.

Rollcall keeps its own file in the repo, [`owners.json`](https://github.com/waynestate/rollcall/blob/main/owners.json): the 13 stack projects the scheduled scan reads, all answered for by the stack maintainer. The repo is public, so its contacts are roles and teams, never a person (a test refuses an `@` in it), and those digests print rather than mail. To scan another fleet, keep that fleet's file next to its snapshots, outside a public repo, and point `ROLLCALL_OWNERS_FILE` there.

An app in the scan that no entry lists is not dropped. `rollcall digest` names it on stderr every run,

```
No owner on file for 1 of 14 apps in this scan, so no digest covers it. Add it to the owners file:
- group/new-project: no owner on file
```

and `--format=json` lists it under `no_owner_on_file`. An owner who has not opted in still counts as its owner. Reports never read the owners file, so the report stays free of owners.

### 2. Print them[#](https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/digest.html#2-print-them)

After a scan:

```
rollcall digest
```

prints one digest per opted-in owner with news, each headed `To:` and `Subject:`. `--owner=CONTACT` picks one owner (an owner who has not opted in is refused), `--format=json` gives a script the same digests (`contract/digest.schema.json`), and `--out=DIR` writes them as `<scan date>-<contact>.txt` instead of printing, for a mail tool you already run. Lines on stderr name any app with no owner on file and count how many owners had news and how many get nothing this time.

What counts as a change, app by app:

- the PHP image moved (a move from end of life to a supported PHP says so, with a well-earned "Present!");
- the declared PHP floor, the Laravel version or the PROCTOR result changed;
- a drift flag appeared ("now runs an end-of-life Laravel") or cleared ("no longer has a failing PROCTOR result"), including one that appears because a date in CREED's policy passed;
- an app answered present for the first time, or was in the last scan and is not in this one.

The first scan has no "before", so the first digest is a first roll call: every app and where it stands. The states and flags are the report's own (`rollcall report --internal`), so a digest and the report never disagree.

### 3. Mail them (only if you want Rollcall to)[#](https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/digest.html#3-mail-them-only-if-you-want-rollcall-to)

Sending is a second, separate switch, and every part of it must be there:

1. `composer require symfony/mailer` (Rollcall only suggests it).
2. `ROLLCALL_DIGEST_MAIL_ENABLED=true`.
3. `ROLLCALL_DIGEST_MAIL_DSN`: a Symfony Mailer DSN, such as `smtp://mail.example.test:25`. It can hold a password, so it is a secret: never in git, never printed.
4. `ROLLCALL_DIGEST_MAIL_FROM`: the from address.
5. `rollcall digest --send`.

Without any one of them nothing is mailed; with the settings but no `--send`, the digests are only printed. Every contact with news must be a mail address, or nothing goes out at all. Mail is plain text. This is the one outbound action in Rollcall, so it stays behind both the flag and the settings.

Schedule it right after `rollcall scan`: weekly suits the burn-down, and a quiet week sends nothing.

---

Source: https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/laravel.html

## Laravel[#](https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/laravel.html#laravel)

This page wires Rollcall into a Laravel app. Next: [use it from your coding agent (ADVISOR)](https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/advisor.html).

The package registers itself (`extra.laravel.providers`). Publish the config with `php artisan vendor:publish --tag=rollcall-config`, set the variables in [the configuration reference](https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/configuration.html), and schedule `rollcall:scan`. The dashboard shows counts and progress; the per-app page is a second route that stays off until you enable it, and it runs behind `rollcall.dashboard.internal_middleware` (default `web` and `auth.sesame`), so an app with no such middleware fails closed. The page uses WayneUI's class names and takes its stylesheet from `ROLLCALL_WAYNEUI_CSS`. The page also carries a status line (a `role="status"` paragraph) that names the apps shown and the scan date, so assistive technology hears what the page displays. The `/metrics` route is registered on its own path; if your app already serves `/metrics` (HELMET does), run Rollcall's on a separate app or leave metrics off.

---

Source: https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/metrics.html

## Metrics[#](https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/metrics.html#metrics)

This page turns on and protects the Prometheus endpoint. Next: [Laravel](https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/laravel.html) for the dashboard.

Metrics are off by default (the stack's metrics rule). With `ROLLCALL_METRICS_ENABLED=true`, `/metrics` serves Prometheus text built from the latest snapshot (a request never triggers a scan). It needs `ROLLCALL_METRICS_TOKEN` as a bearer token or an address in `ROLLCALL_METRICS_ALLOW`; with neither set, nobody gets in. Labels are version numbers, state names, drift kinds and public package names: no app names or personal data. The dashboard JSON is in `grafana/rollcall-burn-down.json`; import it into Grafana once a Prometheus server scrapes the endpoint. Run `rollcall scan` on a schedule so the series moves.

Forced image upgrades from a Citadel export come through as three gauges, counts only, in the same style as the rest: `rollcall_forced_upgrades_pending_apps` (apps with one pending, overdue ones included), `rollcall_forced_upgrades_overdue_apps` (due today or earlier) and `rollcall_forced_upgrades_next_due_timestamp_seconds` (midnight of the next date still ahead, only while there is one). With any other image source the two counts are 0 and the date is absent. The dashboard shows pending and overdue as two stat panels.

**Watch the back row empty (the burn-down, sample data)**

![Rollcall's sample burn-down: hatched bars of apps on an end-of-life PHP image falling from 19 on August 12 to 4 on October 28, with a red line over the top and the last bar filled green.](https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/docs/readme/burn-down.jpg)

The same line Grafana draws from `/metrics`. Made-up apps, real arithmetic.

---

Source: https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/quick-start.html

## Quick start[#](https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/quick-start.html#quick-start)

This page takes you from a fresh clone to a first report, on the fixtures in the repo. Next: read [what the report says](https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/what-the-report-says.html).

This runs on the fixtures in the repo, so you need no network and no token. Run `composer install` once (or the Docker line under [Run the checks](https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/docs/checks.html)), then the commands below.

Linux and macOS (bash):

```
export ROLLCALL_POLICY_FILE=tests/fixtures/policy.json
export ROLLCALL_REPOS_DIR=tests/fixtures/repos
export ROLLCALL_IMAGES_FILE=tests/fixtures/images.json
export ROLLCALL_PROCTOR_DIR=tests/fixtures/proctor
export ROLLCALL_STORE_DIR=var/snapshots
php bin/rollcall scan
php bin/rollcall report
```

Windows (PowerShell, no bash or WSL needed):

```
$env:ROLLCALL_POLICY_FILE = "tests/fixtures/policy.json"
$env:ROLLCALL_REPOS_DIR = "tests/fixtures/repos"
$env:ROLLCALL_IMAGES_FILE = "tests/fixtures/images.json"
$env:ROLLCALL_PROCTOR_DIR = "tests/fixtures/proctor"
$env:ROLLCALL_STORE_DIR = "var/snapshots"
php bin/rollcall scan
php bin/rollcall report
```

`policy.json` is CREED's file; the copy under `tests/fixtures/` is a snapshot for tests. Use the released one in real runs.

---

Source: https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/what-the-report-says.html

## What the report says[#](https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/what-the-report-says.html#what-the-report-says)

This page explains each part of the report. Next: [Citadel's registrations export](https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/citadel.html) if your apps run on Citadel.

- **Apps present and scan notes**: the first line counts the apps the scan read, then the notes it printed and carried on past (`totals.scan_errors` in JSON, `rollcall_scan_errors` in metrics). Today a note means a source is not configured: with no image export the PHP image column is `unknown`, with no PROCTOR reports every app is `none`. `scan` prints each note as it saves the snapshot, and `report --format=json --internal` lists them. A note is not a failed scan; a source that refuses (a bad token) stops the scan instead.
- **PHP image, declared PHP floor, Laravel**: apps per version, the state from the policy (`active`, `security_only`, `eol`, `unknown`), the date security support ends and the days left (negative once past).
- **Auth package and PROCTOR**: apps per auth package, and per PROCTOR result (`pass`, `fail`, `none`).
- **Drift**, counted per kind: `image_eol`, `image_unknown`, `image_below_floor`, `floor_allows_eol`, `floor_unbounded`, `eol_past_grace` (past the policy's grace days), `laravel_eol`, `proctor_missing`, `proctor_failing`, `override_expired`.
- **Progress**: apps that moved since the previous scan and apps that went from an EOL image to a supported one. In the internal view each upgraded app carries the day it landed.
- **EOL burn-down**: for each scan day, how many apps ran an EOL image on that day. It reads the image, not the declared floor, so until an image export is configured every app is `unknown` here even when the floor table already shows EOL versions.
- **The roll per version, scan after scan**: each burn-down day also carries the same apps counted three ways, so a dashboard can chart which lines the fleet is leaving and which it is joining. Counts only, never an app name:
  - `states`: per support state on that day (`active`, `security_only`, `eol`, `unknown`); `supported` is `active` plus `security_only`.
  - `php_image`: per PHP minor of the image, in version order with `unknown` last, such as `{"8.1": 3, "8.4": 9, "unknown": 2}`.
  - `laravel`: per Laravel major, the same way. An app with no Laravel, or one Rollcall could not read, is `unknown`.
  The breakdown is worked out from each stored snapshot when the report is built, so snapshots written before it existed (Rollcall 0.1.9 and older) get one too, and the stored snapshot format is unchanged (`schema_version` 1). It reaches back as far as `rollcall prune` keeps snapshots (`ROLLCALL_RETENTION_DAYS`). A report written by 0.1.9 or older has no `states`, `php_image` or `laravel` on its burn-down days: read that as "no breakdown", not as zero apps.
- **Forced image upgrades**: with [Citadel's export](https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/citadel.html) as the image source, how many apps have a forced base-image upgrade pending, how many are due today or earlier, and the next date (`forced_upgrades`, counts only). The same counts reach [metrics](https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/metrics.html) and ADVISOR's `rollcall_fleet_summary` ([ADVISOR](https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/advisor.html)). The internal per-app list carries each app's `upgrade_due`. All three are zero with any other image source.

State is never decided in code: it is derived from the dates in `policy.json` by CREED's reader. A version the policy does not list is `unknown`.

---

Source: https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/wsu-values.html

## WSU values (Playbook)[#](https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/wsu-values.html#wsu-values-playbook)

This page says which setting may come from Playbook, and how to get Playbook into your app. Next: [Metrics](https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/metrics.html).

`ROLLCALL_GITLAB_URL` is a Wayne State value, so it may come from Playbook (`waynestate/playbook`) when the environment has none. The environment always wins; Playbook only fills what the environment leaves out. The GitLab token never comes through Playbook and stays an environment variable.

| Setting | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `ROLLCALL_GITLAB_URL` | The `https://` base URL of the GitLab instance |

Playbook is private and lives on git.wayne.edu. Getting it into your app:

Composer: add the repository to your `composer.json`, then require the package. Composer authenticates to git.wayne.edu with the token in `auth.json`.

```json
{
    "repositories": [
        {"type": "vcs", "url": "https://git.wayne.edu/enterprise-apps/playbook.git"}
    ]
}
```

```
composer require waynestate/playbook
```

curl (Linux, macOS):

```
curl --fail -H "PRIVATE-TOKEN: $GITLAB_TOKEN" "https://git.wayne.edu/api/v4/projects/enterprise-apps%2Fplaybook/repository/files/playbook.env/raw?ref=main" -o .env.playbook
```

PowerShell (Windows):

```
Invoke-WebRequest -Headers @{ 'PRIVATE-TOKEN' = $env:GITLAB_TOKEN } -Uri "https://git.wayne.edu/api/v4/projects/enterprise-apps%2Fplaybook/repository/files/playbook.env/raw?ref=main" -OutFile .env.playbook
```

Clone:

```
git clone https://git.wayne.edu/enterprise-apps/playbook.git
```

The token is your own: `read_api` for curl, `read_repository` for clone and Composer.

Playbook is private on git.wayne.edu. If you get a 404, ask the Enterprise Applications team for read access.
