Source: https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/docs/

## Rollcall[#](https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/docs/#rollcall)

This page says what Rollcall is and where it sits in the stack. Next: [install it](https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/docs/install.html), then run the [quick start](https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/quick-start.html).

> Every app answers "present". The ones on PHP 7.4 answer from the back row.

Front page: [`site/index.html`](https://github.com/waynestate/rollcall/blob/main/site/index.html). It is static, with no build step (see [`site/README.md`](https://github.com/waynestate/rollcall/blob/main/site/README.md)). On Citadel, the raw-PHP deploy layer in [`deploy/`](https://github.com/waynestate/rollcall/tree/main/deploy) serves it: a Squire kit whose front controller puts `site/` behind HELMET's security headers. For local development, serve `site/` directly.

Rollcall is the fleet scanner for the Wayne State application stack. For each app it records the PHP image, the lowest PHP its `composer.json` allows, the Laravel version, the auth package and its version, the PROCTOR result, and, when the app commits one, the result, Booster version and finish time of Booster's hop record (`booster-hop.json`). Then it looks up each version by date in CREED's `policy.json`. It keeps one snapshot per scan, so you can see drift and an EOL burn-down over time. It prunes old snapshots after the retention window (default 90 days; the newest one always stays).

Rollcall enforces nothing. It never opens an issue, leaves a comment or deploys anything, and it exits `0` whatever the fleet looks like. The public report has totals only: counts and progress, no app names, owners or rankings. The per-app list is internal. Like a good attendance sheet, it is for noticing who is missing, not for shaming them.

![A page of Rollcall's roll book: seventeen sample apps called down the register one at a time, each answered with a stamp: seven present, five late, four back row and one inaudible.](https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/docs/readme/register.svg)
One page of the roll book, called name by name. Sample data: the apps are fictional, and a real scan's per-app list stays internal.

### Where it sits in the stack[#](https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/docs/#where-it-sits-in-the-stack)

The parts of the Wayne State application stack, and their jobs. WELD is the Laravel starter app that has most of them installed:

| Part | Job |
| --- | --- |
| WayneUI (project 0) | The interface layer: tokens, components, four consumer paths |
| CREED | The standards and `policy.json`, the dates Rollcall reads |
| PROCTOR | Measures one app against the policy; Rollcall reads its JSON report and never re-runs a rule |
| Preflight | CI templates |
| SESAME | Protocol-neutral auth; Rollcall reports which auth package each app uses |
| HELMET | Baseline runtime and its own optional `/metrics` |
| Pinstripe | The coding standard this repo includes for its Pint and PHPStan settings |
| Sourdough | Starters |
| Rollcall | The fleet census and EOL burn-down |

**The whole class**
WayneUI and the stack. Everyone is here today; the ones in the back row know who they are.

[![WayneUI](https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/docs/readme/cast/wayneui.png)](https://github.com/waynestate/wayne-ui) [![CREED](https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/docs/readme/cast/creed.png)](https://github.com/waynestate/creed) [![PROCTOR](https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/docs/readme/cast/proctor.png)](https://github.com/waynestate/proctor) [![SESAME](https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/docs/readme/cast/sesame.png)](https://github.com/waynestate/sesame) [![HELMET](https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/docs/readme/cast/helmet.png)](https://github.com/waynestate/helmet) [![Sourdough](https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/docs/readme/cast/sourdough.png)](https://github.com/waynestate/sourdough) [![Squire](https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/docs/readme/cast/squire.png)](https://github.com/waynestate/squire) [![Preflight](https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/docs/readme/cast/preflight.png)](https://github.com/waynestate/preflight) [![Pinstripe](https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/docs/readme/cast/pinstripe.png)](https://github.com/waynestate/pinstripe) [![Booster](https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/docs/readme/cast/booster.png)](https://github.com/waynestate/booster) [![Rollcall](https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/docs/readme/cast/rollcall.png)](https://github.com/waynestate/rollcall) [![Drawbridge](https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/docs/readme/cast/drawbridge.png)](https://git.wayne.edu/enterprise-apps/drawbridge) [![ADVISOR](https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/docs/readme/cast/advisor.png)](https://github.com/waynestate/advisor) [![WELD](https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/docs/readme/cast/weld.png)](https://github.com/waynestate/weld)

Images are regenerated from the front page by [`scripts/readme-art`](https://github.com/waynestate/rollcall/tree/main/scripts/readme-art). Present.

**The brand board (the cover of the book)**

![Rollcall's brand board: the open roll-book mark with a gold tick on a green tile, lockups, the green, gold and cream palette, type, favicons, and do and don't panels.](https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/docs/readme/board.jpg)

### Install[#](https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/docs/#install)

One line:

```
composer require waynestate/rollcall
```

The first command is `php bin/rollcall scan`; the [quick start](https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/quick-start.html) runs it on the fixtures in the repo, and [Install](https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/docs/install.html) has the rest.

## Install[#](https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/docs/install.html#install)

This page is the install. Next: run the [quick start](https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/quick-start.html).

```
composer require waynestate/rollcall
```

Rollcall is on Packagist, so no extra repository is needed. Requires PHP `^8.3`. The CLI is `vendor/bin/rollcall`.

Optional: `composer require symfony/mailer` only if Rollcall should mail the [owner digests](https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/digest.html) itself (`rollcall digest --send`). Printing them, or writing them to files, needs nothing extra.

Source: https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/commands.html

## Commands[#](https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/commands.html#commands)

This page lists the commands (generated from the CLI) and what each one prints, plus the exit codes.

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `rollcall advisories` | Check locked package versions against a saved Packagist security-advisories response. |
| `rollcall digest` | Print (or write, or send) each opted-in owner's digest of what changed in their apps. |
| `rollcall drift` | Compare policy.json with a saved endoflife.date v1 product file. |
| `rollcall prune` | Delete snapshots older than the retention window; the newest is never deleted. |
| `rollcall report` | Print the fleet report from the stored snapshots. |
| `rollcall scan` | Scan the fleet read-only and store a snapshot. |

#### `rollcall advisories` [#](https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/commands.html#rollcall-advisories)

Check locked package versions against a saved Packagist security-advisories response.

Usage: `rollcall advisories [--today TODAY] [--feed FEED]`

| Option | Meaning | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--today=VALUE` | Override today's date (YYYY-MM-DD). |  |
| `--feed=VALUE` | Path to the saved Packagist security-advisories JSON. |  |
| `--silent` | Do not output any message |  |

#### `rollcall digest` [#](https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/commands.html#rollcall-digest)

Print (or write, or send) each opted-in owner's digest of what changed in their apps.

Usage: `rollcall digest [--today TODAY] [--owner OWNER] [--format FORMAT] [--out OUT] [--send]`

| Option | Meaning | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--today=VALUE` | Override today's date (YYYY-MM-DD). |  |
| `--owner=VALUE` | Only this contact from the owners file. |  |
| `--format=VALUE` | text or json. | `text` |
| `--out=VALUE` | Write one text file per digest into this directory instead of printing them. |  |
| `--send` | Mail the digests. Needs ROLLCALL_DIGEST_MAIL_ENABLED=true, ROLLCALL_DIGEST_MAIL_DSN and ROLLCALL_DIGEST_MAIL_FROM. |  |
| `--silent` | Do not output any message |  |

#### `rollcall drift` [#](https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/commands.html#rollcall-drift)

Compare policy.json with a saved endoflife.date v1 product file.

Usage: `rollcall drift [--today TODAY] [--feed FEED] [--component COMPONENT]`

| Option | Meaning | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--today=VALUE` | Override today's date (YYYY-MM-DD). |  |
| `--feed=VALUE` | Path to the saved endoflife.date JSON. |  |
| `--component=VALUE` | Policy component to compare. | `php` |
| `--silent` | Do not output any message |  |

#### `rollcall prune` [#](https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/commands.html#rollcall-prune)

Delete snapshots older than the retention window; the newest is never deleted.

Usage: `rollcall prune [--today TODAY] [--days DAYS] [--dry-run]`

| Option | Meaning | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--today=VALUE` | Override today's date (YYYY-MM-DD). |  |
| `--days=VALUE` | Retention window in days (default: ROLLCALL_RETENTION_DAYS, 90; 0 keeps everything). |  |
| `--dry-run` | List what would be deleted without deleting anything. |  |
| `--silent` | Do not output any message |  |

#### `rollcall report` [#](https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/commands.html#rollcall-report)

Print the fleet report from the stored snapshots.

Usage: `rollcall report [--today TODAY] [--format FORMAT] [--internal]`

| Option | Meaning | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--today=VALUE` | Override today's date (YYYY-MM-DD). |  |
| `--format=VALUE` | text, json or prometheus. | `text` |
| `--internal` | Include the per-app list. Internal only: do not publish it. |  |
| `--silent` | Do not output any message |  |

#### `rollcall scan` [#](https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/commands.html#rollcall-scan)

Scan the fleet read-only and store a snapshot.

Usage: `rollcall scan [--today TODAY] [--prune [PRUNE]]`

| Option | Meaning | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--today=VALUE` | Override today's date (YYYY-MM-DD). |  |
| `--prune=VALUE` | After saving, delete snapshots older than this many days (default: ROLLCALL_RETENTION_DAYS, 90; 0 keeps everything). |  |
| `--silent` | Do not output any message |  |

#### Options every command accepts[#](https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/commands.html#options-every-command-accepts)

| Option | Meaning | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `-h`, `--help` | Display help for the given command. When no command is given display help for the list command |  |
| `-q`, `--quiet` | Only errors are displayed. All other output is suppressed |  |
| \`-v | -vv | -vvv`, `--verbose\` |
| `-V`, `--version` | Display this application version |  |
| `--ansi` | Force (or disable --no-ansi) ANSI output |  |
| `--no-ansi` | Negate the "--ansi" option |  |
| `-n`, `--no-interaction` | Do not ask any interactive question |  |

- `scan` scans once and stores `<ROLLCALL_STORE_DIR>/<date>.json`. A second scan on the same day replaces it. A gap in one source (a missing report, a bad image tag) becomes a note on that app, and the scan carries on. A refused GitLab token stops the scan loudly instead of producing a flattering partial answer. `--prune[=DAYS]` deletes snapshots older than that many days after saving (default: `ROLLCALL_RETENTION_DAYS`, 90; 0 keeps everything).
- `report` prints the latest snapshot against the policy as of today. `text` is a terminal table, `json` is the machine-readable form, `prometheus` is the metrics text (refused unless `ROLLCALL_METRICS_ENABLED=true`). `--internal` adds the per-app list; keep that output inside the project.
- `drift` compares `policy.json` with a saved endoflife.date v1 product page (for example `https://endoflife.date/api/v1/products/php/` saved to a file). A difference is a flag for a person to look at; the policy stays the source of truth. Rollcall does not fetch that page itself.
- `advisories` checks each app's locked `laravel/framework` and auth-package versions against a saved Packagist security-advisories response (for example `https://packagist.org/api/security-advisories/?packages[]=laravel/framework` saved to a file). One line per package and version, sorted by package then version: the status (`affected`, `clear` or `no data`), the count and the advisory ids, and how many apps hold that pair. A package with no advisory data prints `no data`, never `safe`: an absent row proves nothing about the package, and a version nobody can parse says `no data` too. Rollcall does not fetch that page itself; a person saves it and `--feed` points at the file. Output is package names and counts only: no app ids.
- `prune` deletes snapshots older than `--days` (default: `ROLLCALL_RETENTION_DAYS`, 90; 0 keeps everything). The newest snapshot is never deleted, even if it is older than the cut-off, so the dashboard always has data. `--dry-run` lists what would go without deleting anything.

Exit codes: `0` ok, `2` tool error (bad option, unreadable policy, a source that refused). There is no `1`: Rollcall does not gate anything.

---

Source: https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/configuration.html

## Configuration[#](https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/configuration.html#configuration)

This page covers how Rollcall is configured, all through environment variables. Next: [run the collector in Docker](https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/collector-docker.html) with them.

Every setting is an environment variable. `.env.example` holds placeholders; never commit a real token.

| Variable | Meaning | Default | Read in |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ROLLCALL_AUTH_PACKAGES | Comma-separated Composer packages that count as an auth package | the built-in list | config/rollcall.php |
| ROLLCALL_CITADEL_EXPORT | Citadel's saved registrations export, used instead of ROLLCALL_IMAGES_FILE (not both): base images plus forced upgrade dates. See the Citadel guide | none | config/rollcall.php |
| ROLLCALL_DASHBOARD_ENABLED | Laravel: serve the dashboard page | `false` | config/rollcall.php |
| ROLLCALL_DASHBOARD_PATH | Laravel: dashboard URL path | `rollcall` | config/rollcall.php |
| ROLLCALL_DIGEST_MAIL_DSN | Symfony Mailer DSN for sending, such as smtp://mail.example.test:25. A secret: never in git, never printed | none | src/Config.php |
| ROLLCALL_DIGEST_MAIL_ENABLED | Allow `rollcall digest --send` to mail | `false` | src/Config.php |
| ROLLCALL_DIGEST_MAIL_FROM | The from address of the digests | none | src/Config.php |
| ROLLCALL_GITLAB_GROUPS | Comma-separated group ids or paths; subgroups are included. Ignored when ROLLCALL_GITLAB_PROJECTS is set | none | config/rollcall.php |
| ROLLCALL_GITLAB_PROJECTS | Comma-separated full group/project paths; when set, only those projects are scanned and no group is listed | none | config/rollcall.php |
| ROLLCALL_GITLAB_TOKEN | A GitLab group or project access token (a bot), or a service account's token, with the read_api scope only, the Reporter role and an expiry. The stack's is the group token rollcall-scanner, rotated by the stack maintainer (docs/security.md). Never in git, never logged, never printed | none | config/rollcall.php |
| ROLLCALL_GITLAB_URL | https:// base URL of the GitLab instance | none | config/rollcall.php |
| ROLLCALL_IMAGES_FILE | Export of the app list: {"apps": \[{"project": "group/project", "image": "php:8.4-apache"}\]} | none | config/rollcall.php |
| ROLLCALL_INTERNAL_ENABLED | Laravel: serve the per-app page at `<path>/apps` (needs your sign-in middleware) | `false` | config/rollcall.php |
| ROLLCALL_METRICS_ALLOW | Comma-separated scraper IP addresses (exact match) | none | config/rollcall.php |
| ROLLCALL_METRICS_ENABLED | Turn metrics on (CLI report --format=prometheus and /metrics) | `false` | config/rollcall.php |
| ROLLCALL_METRICS_TOKEN | Bearer token a scraper must present | none | config/rollcall.php |
| ROLLCALL_OWNERS_FILE | Owners file for the digests: who answers for which apps, and who opted in with "digest": true. Rollcall's own, for the stack's projects, is owners.json in the repo (roles only); keep another fleet's outside a public repo | none (no digests) | src/Config.php |
| ROLLCALL_POLICY_FILE | Path to CREED's policy.json | none (required for report, drift) | config/rollcall.php |
| ROLLCALL_PROCTOR_DIR | PROCTOR JSON reports, one per app: group/project is read from group\_\_project.json | none | config/rollcall.php |
| ROLLCALL_PUBLIC_REPORT_ENABLED | Serve GET /report.json (public counts only) | `false` | config/rollcall.php |
| ROLLCALL_REPOS_DIR | Fixture repositories as `<group>/<project>/composer.{json,lock}` | none | config/rollcall.php |
| ROLLCALL_RETENTION_DAYS | How many days of snapshots to keep; the newest is never deleted | `90` (0 keeps everything) | config/rollcall.php |
| ROLLCALL_SOURCE | directory (fixtures) or gitlab | `directory` | config/rollcall.php |
| ROLLCALL_STORE_DIR | Snapshot directory, the only place Rollcall writes | `var/snapshots` | config/rollcall.php |
| ROLLCALL_WAYNEUI_CSS | Laravel: https:// or absolute URL of WayneUI's stylesheet for the dashboard | none | config/rollcall.php |

#### Auth packages[#](https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/configuration.html#auth-packages)

`ROLLCALL_AUTH_PACKAGES` is checked in list order, and the first entry that matches an app wins. An entry with a slash matches that package exactly; an entry without a slash is a bare package name and matches that package under any vendor, so `wayne-cas` matches `anyvendor/wayne-cas`. The report carries the real locked package name, vendor included. The built-in list is `waynestate/sesame`, `waynestate/wayne-cas`, `apereo/phpcas`, `jasig/phpcas`, `subfission/cas`, `wayne-cas` and `simplecas`; the exact `waynestate/wayne-cas` entry comes first, so it still wins over the bare `wayne-cas` entry.

To scan GitLab you need the token and either a group or the project allowlist. The narrow way is `ROLLCALL_GITLAB_PROJECTS`: name the exact `group/project` paths and Rollcall reads only those, never listing a group. Otherwise set `ROLLCALL_GITLAB_GROUPS`. The token is a GitLab bot or personal access token with `read_api` only and an expiry, whose user can read only the projects to scan; until it exists Rollcall runs on its fixtures. Set `ROLLCALL_SOURCE=gitlab` and the GitLab variables. The `rollcall-scan` job in `.gitlab-ci.yml` does this on a schedule or by hand. Rollcall sends only `GET` and `HEAD`, fetches the two Composer files without cloning, skips a file whose blob id has not changed, follows `Link` pagination only to the configured host, and waits out `429 Retry-After`.

---

Source: https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/contract.html

## Contract[#](https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/contract.html#contract)

This page covers the shapes Rollcall promises to anyone who reads its output. Next: the [Proof](https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/proof.html) of a real run.

The contract lives in [`contract/`](https://github.com/waynestate/rollcall/tree/main/contract) as JSON Schema (draft 2020-12). `tests/ContractTest.php` runs the real commands on the fixtures, then validates what they print and store against these files, so the code and the contract cannot drift apart. A dashboard, a Grafana import, ADVISOR or a script should read Rollcall against these schemas, not against an example it once saw.

| Schema | What it describes | Who produces it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `report.schema.json` | `rollcall report --format=json` and `GET /report.json`, public and internal views | Rollcall |
| `snapshot.schema.json` | One stored scan, `<ROLLCALL_STORE_DIR>/<date>.json` (internal: it holds app ids) | Rollcall |
| `images-export.schema.json` | The image list behind `ROLLCALL_IMAGES_FILE` | Any platform, or a hand-kept file |
| `citadel-export.schema.json` | The Citadel registrations export behind `ROLLCALL_CITADEL_EXPORT` | A person or a job, from Citadel |
| `owners.schema.json` | The owners file behind `ROLLCALL_OWNERS_FILE`: Rollcall's own `owners.json` (roles only) or a fleet's own (internal) | The people who run Rollcall |
| `digest.schema.json` | `rollcall digest --format=json` (internal: it names apps) | Rollcall |

### What the suite checks[#](https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/contract.html#what-the-suite-checks)

- The public and internal JSON reports, after one scan and after two, match `report.schema.json`.
- `GET /report.json` from the raw-PHP endpoint matches the same schema.
- Every stored snapshot matches `snapshot.schema.json`, and its `schema_version` equals the code's.
- The image list, Citadel export and owners fixtures, and Rollcall's own `owners.json`, match their input schemas, a report and snapshot built from the Citadel export match theirs, and `rollcall digest --format=json` matches `digest.schema.json`.
- The drift kinds in the schema are exactly the ones the report builder counts, in the same order.
- The schema has teeth: a public report with a per-app list, an `owner` field or a made-up drift kind is refused, and so is an internal report without its list.

It reads fixtures only and never calls GitLab, Citadel or any other host. Run it alone with `vendor/bin/phpunit tests/ContractTest.php`; `composer ci` runs it with everything else.

### Rules[#](https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/contract.html#rules)

- **Closed objects.** Rollcall's own output uses `additionalProperties: false` throughout, so a new field is a contract change made in the same commit as the code. Inputs stay open: a producer may add fields of its own, and Rollcall ignores them.
- **Public means counts.** The public report may never carry `apps` or `scan_errors`, and no field holds an owner, a rank or a score.
- **Versioning.** From 1.0.0 on, Rollcall follows SemVer against this contract: an added field or enum value is a minor release; a removed or renamed field or a changed type is a major release. A snapshot carries its own `schema_version` (1 today), and a reader refuses a version it does not know.

---

Source: https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/proof.html

## Proof[#](https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/proof.html#proof)

This page says how Rollcall was proven on real repositories: what ran, what held, what the runs caught in Rollcall itself, and what they do not prove yet. Next, see [What the report says](https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/what-the-report-says.html) for how to read the output quoted here.

A register is only worth something on a day with real students in the room. Rollcall had two such days on 2026-11-06.

### Last run[#](https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/proof.html#last-run)

| Check | Date | Commit | Result | Duration |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `composer ci` | 2026-11-07 | `aed8dd9` | pass: manifest, 199 tests / 1220 assertions, style, generated files, static analysis, audit | 181.3 s |
| `rollcall scan` | 2026-11-07 | `aed8dd9` | pass: 4 fixture apps present, 2 notes (no image source, no PROCTOR reports) | 1.1 s |
| `rollcall report` | 2026-11-07 | `aed8dd9` | pass: text report, 4 apps | 1.0 s |
| `rollcall report --format=json` | 2026-11-07 | `aed8dd9` | pass: JSON report, 4 apps | 1.0 s |
| `rollcall report --format=json --internal` | 2026-11-07 | `aed8dd9` | pass: internal JSON, 4 apps | 1.0 s |
| `rollcall report --format=prometheus` | 2026-11-07 | `aed8dd9` | pass: Prometheus text, 4 apps | 1.2 s |
| `rollcall advisories` (saved feed) | 2026-11-07 | `aed8dd9` | pass: 4 package versions answered, 1 affected, 1 no data | 1.8 s |
| `rollcall drift --component=php` (saved feed) | 2026-11-07 | `aed8dd9` | pass: 1 PHP date compared, 1 difference between the feeds | 1.5 s |
| `rollcall prune --dry-run` | 2026-11-07 | `aed8dd9` | pass: nothing to prune | 1.2 s |
| PROCTOR check on `deploy/` | 2026-11-07 | `aed8dd9` | pass: 14 checks, 12 pass, 2 warn (php-floor, ci-pipelines) | 2.2 s |

The rollcall rows ran against the fixtures bundled under `tests/fixtures/` in one `composer:2.10.3` container, with no credentials; the PROCTOR row installed the deploy layer's committed lock first. To refresh this table, re-run `composer ci` and the commands above and rewrite the rows with the new date, commit and durations. The two runs the page describes, the scheduled GitLab CI scan and the 58-repository corpus rerun, need a live service account and the stack's proof corpus, so they are not repeated here; their results stand as recorded below.

### What ran[#](https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/proof.html#what-ran)

**1. The scheduled scan on GitLab CI.** The weekly `rollcall-scan` job (see [Configuration](https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/configuration.html)) ran on its schedule for the first time, on the canonical GitLab, against the 13 stack projects. It used a read-only service account that can see those 13 projects and nothing else, with a `read_api` token held in a masked CI variable. Rollcall 0.1.9 from `main`, `composer:2.10.3`, no image export and no PROCTOR reports configured.

**2. A rerun over the stack's proof corpus.** The shared corpus is every PHP repository in the stack's census of Wayne State applications: 95 repositories, of which 58 have a `composer.json` (54 with a `composer.lock`). Rollcall's directory source reads exactly those two files, so only those two files were copied out of a Linux checkout of each repository. The rerun used the same Rollcall commit plus the change described below, CREED's released `policy.json`, and `--today=2026-11-06`, in one `composer:2.10.3` container with no network:

1. `rollcall scan`, then `rollcall report` as text, JSON, internal JSON and Prometheus text;
2. `rollcall advisories` against a saved Packagist security-advisories response for `laravel/framework` and the known auth packages;
3. `rollcall drift --component=php` against a saved endoflife.date page for PHP;
4. `rollcall prune --dry-run`.

The 13 stack projects were scanned the same way from their committed files, as a cross-check on the CI run.

A run **passes** when every command exits 0 and every repository with a `composer.json` gets a row. A **tool error** is Rollcall breaking: a crash, an exit 2, a repository silently missing from the snapshot, or a number that disagrees with the files.

### Results[#](https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/proof.html#results)

| Run | Read | Rows | Tool errors | Time |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| CI schedule | 13 stack projects | 13 | 0 | 23 s job, 11 s scan |
| Rerun: stack | 13 stack projects | 13 | 0 | 1.3 s scan |
| Rerun: corpus | 58 repositories | 58 | 0 | 1.4 s scan |

The CI job's 23 seconds include installing Rollcall; the scan itself, 26 file reads over the GitLab API, took about 11. Each report over the corpus took under 4 seconds.

- **The CI scan read exactly what is committed.** The snapshot records the Git blob id of every file it read, and each id matched `main` of its project. The local rerun of the same 13 projects gave the same answer: every project declares a PHP floor of 8.3, and one of them (WELD) locks Laravel 13 and SESAME as its auth package. That is the fleet the stack wants every app to look like: one row, one floor, no back row.
- **Every corpus repository answered.** All 58 got a row with its declared PHP floor, Laravel line (18 of them run Laravel, from 5.8 to 13) and auth package. The ones with no PHP constraint at all are counted as unbounded, not guessed.
- **Advisories answered for every Laravel version** in the corpus from the saved feed, and said `no data` for the in-house packages Packagist has never heard of, including two locked to a development branch. That is the documented behavior: an absent row is never reported as safe.
- **Drift:** CREED's policy and endoflife.date agree on every PHP date they both state.
- **Prune** found nothing to prune, as it should with one fresh snapshot.
- The fleet tallies themselves (how many apps sit on which version) stay with the stack team, the same way Rollcall keeps its own per-app list internal.

### The warning on the scheduled pipeline[#](https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/proof.html#the-warning-on-the-scheduled-pipeline)

The pipeline that ran the scan finished green with one warning. It was not the scan: it was the allowed-to-fail PROCTOR job that checks the front page's own deploy layer (`deploy/`). Run again locally it says:

- `composer-audit` **fail**: the deploy layer's lock held `symfony/http-foundation` and `symfony/yaml` 7.4.22, with five security advisories between them. Symfony 7.4.23 fixes them, and the deploy lock moved to it the same night.
- `ci-pipelines` **warn**: `deploy/` has no `.gitlab-ci.yml`. True and harmless: the pipeline lives at the repository root.
- `php-floor` **warn**: PHP 8.3 is in security-only support until 2027-12-31.

So the one warning on Rollcall's first real attendance day was Rollcall's own homework, found by PROCTOR, which is the system working.

### What it caught in Rollcall[#](https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/proof.html#what-it-caught-in-rollcall)

A run that only finds praise was not looking hard enough. Every finding here is about Rollcall, not the apps:

- **Confirmed fixed: in-house auth packages.** The first corpus run, on 2026-11-03, counted no auth package for any app, because the built-in list only knew public package names and most of the fleet uses an in-house CAS client under a private vendor name. A bare name in `ROLLCALL_AUTH_PACKAGES` now matches under any vendor. This rerun recognized an auth package in 37 of the 58 repositories, as three packages under two vendor names, and named each with its real vendor.
- **Fixed: "scan problems" that were not problems.** The text report's first line said `scan problems: 2` on every run that had no image export and no PROCTOR reports. The 2026-11-03 run took those for two unexplained scan errors and logged them for a look. They are the two notes `scan` prints when a source is not configured. The line now says `scan notes`, and [What the report says](https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/what-the-report-says.html) explains the count. The JSON key and the metric keep their names, so nothing that reads them breaks.
- **Documented: the burn-down needs the image export.** The EOL burn-down counts apps by the PHP image they run. With no image export every app is `unknown` in it, even while the declared-floor table already shows end-of-life versions. That is the design (a floor is a promise, an image is a fact), and the guide now says so.

### What this does not prove[#](https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/proof.html#what-this-does-not-prove)

- **No PHP image column yet.** No export of the runtime image per app exists yet, so the image table, the image drift kinds and the burn-down were all `unknown`. Rollcall's image source is tested on fixtures only.
- **No PROCTOR column yet.** No PROCTOR reports were fed in, so every app shows `none`. The report source is tested on fixtures only.
- **The CI scan covers the stack, not the fleet.** The service account sees the 13 stack projects on purpose. The corpus run covers the fleet, but from copied files, not through the GitLab API.
- **One week, one snapshot.** Drift between scans, upgrade credit and pruning only show over weeks of scheduled runs. They are covered by tests, not yet by a real history.
- **The advisory and endoflife.date feeds were saved on 2026-11-06.** Their answers are only as fresh as the file a person saved.

### Run it on your own repositories[#](https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/proof.html#run-it-on-your-own-repositories)

On a folder of repositories laid out as `<group>/<project>/composer.{json,lock}`:

Linux / macOS

```sh
export ROLLCALL_POLICY_FILE=/path/to/creed/policy.json
export ROLLCALL_REPOS_DIR=/path/to/repos
php bin/rollcall scan
php bin/rollcall report
```

Windows

```powershell
$env:ROLLCALL_POLICY_FILE = "C:\path\to\creed\policy.json"
$env:ROLLCALL_REPOS_DIR = "C:\path\to\repos"
php bin/rollcall scan
php bin/rollcall report
```

To scan your GitLab on a schedule instead, follow [Configuration](https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/configuration.html) and the scheduled scan section of the README. Keep `report --internal` output inside your team.

## Scripts on every OS[#](https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/scripts.html#scripts-on-every-os)

This page lists every script Rollcall ships and how each OS runs it. Next: the [contract](https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/contract.html) its output keeps.

Every developer tool works on Windows, macOS and Linux. Where PHP fits, there is one PHP command and nothing to pair. Where a script drives Docker, it ships twice: a `.ps1` for Windows (PowerShell 5.1 and 7, never bash or WSL) and a `.sh` for Linux and macOS (written for macOS's bash 3.2 and BSD tools). `tests/ScriptPairsTest.php` fails if a script ships without its twin, if a `.sh` uses a bash 4 feature or a GNU-only flag, or if a `.ps1` calls a Unix shell on the host.

### One PHP command, every OS[#](https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/scripts.html#one-php-command-every-os)

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `php bin/rollcall` (`vendor/bin/rollcall` in an install) | The CLI: `scan`, `report`, `digest`, `drift`, `advisories`, `prune` |
| `php bin/docs-site.php` (`composer docs`) | Builds the docs site from `docs/` |
| `php bin/agent-ready.php` (`composer site:agent-ready`) | Writes the Markdown twins, `llms.txt` and the sitemap |
| `php tools/versions-table.php` (`composer site:versions`) | Regenerates the front page versions table from CREED's policy |
| `php tools/creed-copy-check.php` (`composer creed-copy:check`) | Proves the CREED copy has not drifted |

### A pair per OS[#](https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/scripts.html#a-pair-per-os)

| Windows (PowerShell) | Linux and macOS (bash) | What they do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `scripts/a11y.ps1` | `scripts/a11y.sh` | The front page accessibility gate: axe-core in Playwright, in Docker |
| `deploy/scripts/parity.ps1` | `deploy/scripts/parity.sh` | Runs the front page locally on the Citadel PHP image behind a proxy (Squire's) |

`scripts/readme-art` is a Node tool (`npm run build`), the same on every OS.

### Inside Citadel's container only[#](https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/scripts.html#inside-citadel-s-container-only)

These run on Citadel's Linux container, never on a developer machine, so they have no Windows twin. Squire writes and owns them (`deploy/.squire.json`):

| File | When Citadel runs it |
| --- | --- |
| `deploy/build.sh` | At image build time, as root, with `/bin/sh` |
| `deploy/deployments/001-first-release.sh` | Once, when the first release starts |
| `deploy/scripts/release.sh` | After every Quick Update (the post-script), and from the first-release hook |

### Inside GitLab CI only[#](https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/scripts.html#inside-gitlab-ci-only)

This runs in a GitLab CI job on the Linux composer image, never on a developer machine, so it has no Windows twin. It still keeps to POSIX sh and macOS-safe tools, like every `.sh` here.

| File | When GitLab runs it |
| --- | --- |
| `tools/creed-copy-refresh.sh` | The weekly `creed-copy-refresh` job (or a web pipeline on main): re-exports the CREED copy from CREED main, rebuilds the versions table, docs and agent-ready files, runs `composer creed-copy:check` and `composer ci`, and pushes to main with the job token only when both pass |

Before a release, a maintainer runs the smoke test on all three OSes; the checklist is in [MAINTAINING.md](https://github.com/waynestate/rollcall/blob/main/MAINTAINING.md), "Smoke test on every OS".

Source: https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/docs/security.html

## Security notes[#](https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/docs/security.html#security-notes)

This page lists how Rollcall keeps itself and the fleet safe, and exactly what its GitLab token needs. Next: [run the checks](https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/docs/checks.html).

- Read-only toward GitLab and everything else: one gate in the GitLab adapter allows only `GET` and `HEAD`, and a test fails if a write verb appears in `src/`.
- The GitLab token is a group or project access token (a GitLab bot), or a service account's personal access token, with the `read_api` scope only, the Reporter role and an expiry. The stack's own is the group access token `rollcall-scanner` (see [the scanner token and how to rotate it](https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/docs/security.html#the-scanner-token-and-how-to-rotate-it)). It goes in the environment as `ROLLCALL_GITLAB_TOKEN`, never in git, is sent only to the configured `https` host, and is hidden from debug output and error messages. When the source is GitLab, `scan` reads the token's own record (`GET /api/v4/personal_access_tokens/self`) and prints a note 14 days before it expires, or when it has already expired. The note names the date; the stack maintainer rotates the token before its expiry, never Rollcall. The check is advisory: a refused, unreachable or unparseable answer prints nothing and never fails the scan, and the token value never appears in output.
- Composer files are parsed as data. No `composer install`, script or plugin from a scanned repository ever runs.
- PROCTOR reports, image tags and app ids are outside input: shapes are validated, text is bounded, and terminal output strips control characters.

### The GitLab token, exactly[#](https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/docs/security.html#the-gitlab-token-exactly)

Rollcall needs one scope, `read_api`, and one role, Reporter, on each project it scans. Nothing else. GitLab describes `read_api` as read access to the API for the token's scope, and every call Rollcall makes is a read through the REST API.

#### Every call Rollcall makes[#](https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/docs/security.html#every-call-rollcall-makes)

| Call | When | Why | Covered by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `GET /api/v4/groups/:id/projects?include_subgroups=true&simple=true&archived=false&per_page=100` | `ROLLCALL_GITLAB_GROUPS` is set and `ROLLCALL_GITLAB_PROJECTS` is not | Lists the projects to scan, following `Link` pagination to the same host | `read_api` |
| `GET /api/v4/projects/:id?simple=true` | `ROLLCALL_GITLAB_PROJECTS` is set (no group is listed) | Reads each named project's id and default branch | `read_api` |
| `HEAD /api/v4/projects/:id/repository/files/:file_path?ref=` | Every scan, for `composer.json` and `composer.lock` | Reads the blob id only, so an unchanged file is not fetched again | `read_api` |
| `GET /api/v4/projects/:id/repository/files/:file_path/raw?ref=` | When a file is new or changed | Reads the file's bytes, without cloning | `read_api` |
| `GET /api/v4/personal_access_tokens/self` | Every scan | Reads the token's own expiry date for the 14-day note (advisory) | any valid token |

`tests/TokenScopeDocsTest.php` fails if the GitLab adapter calls an API path this table does not list.

#### Scopes it must not have[#](https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/docs/security.html#scopes-it-must-not-have)

| Scope | Why not |
| --- | --- |
| `api` | Read and write access to the whole API. Rollcall never writes, so a leaked `api` token would hand out powers Rollcall never uses |
| `write_repository` | Push access. Rollcall never pushes |
| `read_repository` | Git-over-HTTP pull. Rollcall never clones; it reads two files through the API, which `read_api` covers |
| `read_user` | The `/user` profile. Rollcall never reads a profile; the expiry note uses `personal_access_tokens/self` |
| `read_registry`, `read_virtual_registry` | Container and package registries. Rollcall reads no images; the image tag comes from an export |
| `self_rotate` | Lets the token rotate itself. The stack maintainer rotates the token, never Rollcall |
| `create_runner`, `manage_runner`, `k8s_proxy`, `ai_features` and any admin scope | Nothing Rollcall does |

#### Role, membership and expiry[#](https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/docs/security.html#role-membership-and-expiry)

- **Reporter, on each project to scan, and nothing more.** Reporter is the lowest role that can read a private project's files; Guest cannot. Developer and above add powers Rollcall never uses.
- **Membership is the real fence.** `ROLLCALL_GITLAB_PROJECTS` limits what Rollcall asks for, not what the token can read. A group token reads every project in its group. For the tightest fence, the token's user is a member of just the projects to scan: a service account, or a bot on a small group made for the purpose. The stack's own token takes the wider road on purpose (below), and the scan job's project list keeps the asking narrow.
- **An expiry, always.** GitLab caps a token at 365 days by default. `scan` prints a note 14 days before the expiry and again once it has passed, naming the date.
- **Where it lives.** In the environment of the job that scans, as `ROLLCALL_GITLAB_TOKEN`: on GitLab CI a masked, hidden and protected CI/CD variable on the Rollcall project, not a file variable. Never in git, `.env.example`, an image or a log.
- **Who rotates it.** A role, not a person: the stack maintainer creates the replacement, updates the variable and revokes the old token before the expiry date. Rollcall only reminds.
- **A refused token stops the scan.** A `401` or `403` ends the scan loudly with exit `2`, so a dead token never produces a flattering partial roll.

### The scanner token and how to rotate it[#](https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/docs/security.html#the-scanner-token-and-how-to-rotate-it)

The stack's weekly scan on git.wayne.edu reads with one token. Everything about it except its value is here.

| What | The stack's answer |
| --- | --- |
| Token | The group access token `rollcall-scanner` on the `enterprise-apps` group: Reporter, `read_api` only. The project owner chose group reach (2026-11-06), so it can read the group's projects; the job asks only for the 13 it lists |
| Where it lives | Its value lives only in the CI/CD variable `ROLLCALL_GITLAB_TOKEN` on `enterprise-apps/rollcall`: masked, hidden, protected, not a file. The token itself is listed under the group's Settings > Access tokens |
| Expires | 2027-11-06. `scan` starts its note on 2027-10-23 |
| Who rotates it | The stack maintainer, a role, not a named person. Creating a group access token needs the Owner role on the group; a stack maintainer without it asks a group Owner for step 1 and does the rest |
| What uses it | The `rollcall-scan` job, on the Monday schedule with `ROLLCALL_JOB=scan`, or started by hand |

Rotate it in one sitting, well before the expiry and not just before the Monday schedule runs:

1. **Make the replacement.** In the group's Settings > Access tokens, add a new token: name `rollcall-scanner`, role Reporter, scope `read_api` only, an expiry at most a year out. Copy the value once; GitLab never shows it again. (The token list's Rotate button is the shortcut, but it revokes the old token at once and you must check the new expiry it gives: GitLab's API defaults a rotated token to one week.)
2. **Update the variable.** In `enterprise-apps/rollcall`, Settings > CI/CD > Variables, edit `ROLLCALL_GITLAB_TOKEN` and paste the new value. Keep it masked, hidden and protected, not a file. Paste it nowhere else: not a chat, a ticket, a file or a commit.
3. **Prove it.** Run a pipeline on `main` with the variable `ROLLCALL_JOB` set to `scan`. In the job log, look for `Present: 13 apps.` and no `not set; skipping`, no `GitLab refused the token` and no `Note: the GitLab token` line (the new token is a year from expiry, so it gets no note).
4. **Revoke the old one.** Back in the group's access tokens, revoke the old `rollcall-scanner` (the one with the earlier expiry).
5. **Write down the new date.** Change the expiry in the table above, and note the rotation in `CHANGELOG.md`, in the same merge request.

A token that leaked is rotated the same way, at once, without waiting for its date. Revoking it first is fine: the scan stops loudly until step 2 is done.
